1password.com.name: 1Password
1password.com.description: 1Password makes password and access management software for individuals, families and companies. It was founded in Toronto in 2005 by Dave Teare and Roustem Karimov and is still headquartered there, with David Faugno as chief executive. The company says more than 200,000 businesses use its products, and its business range now covers privileged access, device trust and the management of SaaS applications alongside the core password manager. It reports more than 1,400 employees and $400 million in annual recurring revenue.

a24films.com.name: A24
a24films.com.description: A24 is a New York studio that finances, produces and distributes feature films and makes television series. It was founded in 2012 by Daniel Katz, David Fenkel and John Hodges, and its films include Moonlight, Uncut Gems and Everything Everywhere All at Once. On television it has made Euphoria and Beef. The company also owns the Cherry Lane Theatre in New York, and a 2024 funding round led by Thrive Capital valued it at $3.5 billion.

acko.com.name: ACKO
acko.com.description: ACKO sells general and life insurance to Indian customers through its website and app, and also offers group health cover for employers. It was founded in Bengaluru in 2016, and the group runs Acko General Insurance and Acko Life Insurance under the holding company Acko Technology and Services. Its general insurance arm reported a net profit of ₹43.6 crore for FY26. The company has appointed bankers for a planned stock market listing, with a target of the first half of 2027.

acorns.com.name: Acorns
acorns.com.description: Acorns is a US consumer finance app for saving and investing small amounts over time. Alongside its round-up investing account, it offers an IRA retirement account called Later, Mighty Oak checking, an emergency savings account and Acorns Early for investing on behalf of children. The company was started by Walter and Jeff Cruttenden and is based in Irvine, California. It bought the children's money app GoHenry in 2023 and says it has served more than 16 million customers in total.

andela.com.name: Andela
andela.com.description: Andela recruits, vets and places software engineers and other technologists with employers, either as individual hires or as fully managed teams. It was founded in 2014 by a group that included Jeremy Johnson and Iyinoluwa Aboyeji, and Carrol Chang has been chief executive since September 2024. The company says its talent network reaches more than 135 countries and that it has served over 650 clients. Its newer services centre on AI engineering assessment, training and delivery, and it owns the coding challenge site Codewars, bought in 2023.

apna.co.name: apna
apna.co.description: apna runs a mobile app and website where job seekers in India look for work in roles such as field sales, accounts and telecalling, and where employers post vacancies and screen applicants. Nirmit Parikh launched it in December 2019, and a $100 million funding round in 2021 gave it unicorn status. The company says it connects more than 5.9 crore job seekers with about 7 lakh employers. For the year to March 2025 it reported operating revenue of ₹122 crore.

babbel.com.name: Babbel
babbel.com.description: Babbel sells subscription language courses through its app, along with podcasts, games and an AI conversation practice tool called Babbel Speak. The company traces its origins to 2007 and was founded by Markus Witte, Thomas Holl, Lorenz Heine and Toine Diepstraten. It has offices in Berlin and New York and says it has sold more than 30 million subscriptions. Its courses cover more than a dozen languages, among them Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and Turkish, and its staff come from more than 80 nationalities.

backmarket.com.name: Back Market
backmarket.com.description: Back Market runs an online marketplace where screened professional refurbishers sell reconditioned phones, laptops, tablets, games consoles and home appliances. It was founded in Paris in 2014 by Thibaud Hug de Larauze, Quentin Le Brouster and Vianney Vaute, has raised over $1 billion from investors and now operates in 17 countries. Besides device sales it offers trade-in for old devices, BackUp protection plans and a purchasing service for businesses. Former finance chief Clément Petit became chief executive in September 2026, with Hug de Larauze staying on as executive chairman.

baemin.com.name: Baemin
products: Baemin Sajangnim app for restaurant owners
Baemin Connect app for delivery riders
baemin.com.description: Baemin, short for Baedal Minjok, is the delivery app of Woowa Brothers, a company Kim Bong-jin started in Seoul in 2010 as a five-person team, launching the app the same year. It is South Korea's largest food delivery platform and also runs a Baemin Club membership, separate apps for restaurant owners and delivery riders, and a wholesale ingredient store for restaurants. Woowa Brothers is a wholly owned subsidiary of Delivery Hero. Uber agreed in July 2026 to buy Delivery Hero, and the deal, still awaiting regulatory approval, would bring Baemin under Uber.
baemin.com.status: Active. Parent Delivery Hero agreed in July 2026 to be acquired by Uber, pending approvals

bamboohr.com.name: BambooHR
bamboohr.com.description: BambooHR was started in 2008 in Lindon, Utah, by Ben Peterson and Ryan Sanders, and sells cloud HR software to small and mid-sized employers. The platform keeps employee records and handles applicant tracking, onboarding and time off, and in 2023 the company added fully integrated payroll and benefits administration. It reports about 33,000 customers and 3 million users, and had grown to roughly 1,200 staff by 2023. Brad Rencher has been chief executive since 2019, with both founders still listed in the leadership team.

bayt.com.name: Bayt.com
bayt.com.description: Bayt.com has run an online job site for the Middle East and North Africa from Dubai since 2000. It was founded by Rabea Ataya, still its chief executive, with co-founder Akram Assaf, who serves as chief technology officer. Job seekers apply to vacancies posted by employers, who also pay for job postings and searches of its CV database. The company says over 53 million professionals and 60,000 employers use the site, served from 11 regional offices, and it also organises career fairs, training workshops and graduate surveys.

bayut.com.name: Bayut
products: Property listings for sale and rent
bayut.com.description: Bayut has listed UAE property for sale and rent since 2008, covering all seven emirates from Dubai and Abu Dhabi to Fujairah. Alongside listings it offers TruCheck listing verification, TruEstimate price estimates, Dubai Land Department transaction records, area guides and an AI search assistant called BayutGPT, plus a portal for estate agents. Bayut belongs to Dubai-based Dubizzle Group, which also runs dubizzle and reports about 18 million monthly users across its platforms. The group announced a Dubai Financial Market listing in October 2025 but postponed it the day before subscriptions were due to open.

betterment.com.name: Betterment
betterment.com.description: Betterment was co-founded in 2008 by Jon Stein and Eli Broverman and began offering automated investment advice in 2010. From its New York base it builds and rebalances portfolios for individual savers and also provides IRAs, Solo 401(k)s, checking, a high-yield cash account and crypto portfolios. Betterment at Work sells 401(k) plans to employers, and Advisor Solutions serves independent financial advisers. The company reports more than $70 billion in assets and over 1 million customers, and in 2025 it bought Ellevest's automated investing business and the software firm Rowboat Advisors.

bharatpe.com.name: BharatPe
bharatpe.com.description: BharatPe was set up in 2018 by Bhavik Koladiya and Shashvat Nakrani, with Ashneer Grover joining as co-founder and chief executive later that year. It gives Indian shopkeepers QR codes that accept UPI payments, along with card machines, payment speakers and loans linked to their daily takings, and it runs a consumer UPI app. The company says it serves more than 10 million merchants in over 400 cities. In July 2026 it renamed its lending company Trillionloans as BharatPe Capital, and it also holds a stake in Unity Small Finance Bank. Nalin Negi is chief executive.

bird.co.name: Bird
bird.co.markets: 200+ cities in North America, Europe and the Middle East
bird.co.description: Bird was started in Santa Monica, California, in 2017 by Travis VanderZanden, a former Uber and Lyft executive, and rents dockless electric scooters and e-bikes through its app. After a Chapter 11 bankruptcy its assets were sold to the newly formed Third Lane Mobility, which also owns the Spin brand, and the business left bankruptcy in April 2024. Third Lane runs scooter and bike programmes in more than 200 cities and raised $20 million in January 2026 to put about 35,000 more vehicles on the road. Stewart Lyons is Bird's chief executive.
bird.co.status: Active. Emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy in April 2024 under new owner Third Lane Mobility

bitdefender.com.name: Bitdefender
bitdefender.com.description: Bitdefender was founded in Romania in 2001 by Florin Talpes, still its chief executive, and his wife Mariuca, and grew out of Softwin, a software firm created in 1990. It is run from Bucharest, with a US headquarters in Santa Clara, California, and sells security software for home users as well as endpoint protection, email security and managed detection and response for businesses. The company has more than 1,600 staff and sells through over 41,000 channel and MSP partners to customers in 170 countries. Private equity firm Vitruvian Partners invested in 2017.

bitflyer.com.name: bitFlyer
products: bitFlyer Prime and API for corporate users
bitflyer.com.description: bitFlyer, Inc. was set up in Tokyo in January 2014 and is registered with the Kanto Local Finance Bureau as crypto-asset exchange service provider No. 00003. Customers can buy and sell bitcoin and other crypto assets directly, trade on the bitFlyer Lightning platform or set up recurring purchases, while corporate users get bitFlyer Prime and an API. Its parent, bitFlyer Holdings, also runs bitFlyer USA and bitFlyer Europe, and in July 2024 bought FTX Japan to build a custody business for institutions. Co-founder Yuzo Kano is chief executive.

bithumb.com.name: Bithumb
products: Crypto spot trading in Korean won
bithumb.com.description: Bithumb opened in January 2014 under the name Xcoin, took its current name in July 2015 and operates from Seoul. It runs a spot exchange where customers trade more than 440 digital assets against the Korean won, and also offers automated trading, staking and deposit services. Bithumb Holdings owns 73.56% of the exchange operator. In an August 2026 customer notice the company said it aims to list on the Korean stock market in 2028, after strengthening internal controls and moving to Korean IFRS accounting standards.
bithumb.com.status: Active. Plans a Korean stock market listing in 2028

bitpanda.com.name: Bitpanda
bitpanda.com.description: Bitpanda was founded in Vienna in 2014 by Eric Demuth, Paul Klanschek and Christian Trummer, and its app lets European retail investors trade crypto, gold and silver, and stocks, with more than 10,000 assets available. It gained a licence under the EU's MiCA rules in 2025, runs Bitpanda Custody for institutions after buying Trustology in 2022, and offers its trading infrastructure to other businesses. The holding company, Bitpanda Group AG, is registered in Zürich, and staff of over 800 work from Vienna, Berlin and Barcelona. A planned Frankfurt listing was put on hold in September 2026, when Trummer became co-chief executive.
bitpanda.com.status: Active. Planned Frankfurt IPO on hold since September 2026

bitso.com.name: Bitso
bitso.com.description: Bitso was founded in 2014 and offers crypto trading, earning and payment services to more than 10 million users in Mexico, Brazil, Argentina and Colombia. Its consumer app also gives access to equities and other investment products, while Bitso Business handles local and cross-border payments for over 1,900 institutional clients. The group also owns Nvío, Nvierte and Juno, and provides institutional connectivity in Chile, Peru, the United States and Europe. Co-founder Daniel Vogel is chief executive, and the company hosted its Stablecoin Conference in Mexico City in June 2026.

bitvavo.com.name: Bitvavo
products: Crypto buying and selling in euros
bitvavo.com.description: Bitvavo B.V. was founded in the Netherlands in 2018 and runs a crypto platform where retail investors and professional traders buy, sell and store digital assets in euros. The Dutch regulator, the AFM, authorised it as a crypto-asset service provider under the EU's MiCA regulation in 2025, allowing it to serve customers across the European Union. By mid-2025 the company reported nearly 2 million users, about 450 staff and a 50% share of euro spot crypto trading. It is registered with the Dutch Chamber of Commerce under number 68743424.

blablacar.com.name: BlaBlaCar
blablacar.com.description: BlaBlaCar connects drivers who have empty seats with passengers heading the same way, and sells bus and train tickets in the same app. It was founded in 2006 by Frédéric Mazzella, Francis Nappez and Nicolas Brusson, who is now chief executive, and is operated by Comuto SA from Paris. The company says about 40 million members travel with it each year across 41 countries, with more than 6,000 bus operators on the platform. It bought Busfor and Octobus, whose software digitises ticketing for bus stations and coach companies, and employs about 800 people.

boat-lifestyle.com.name: boAt
boat-lifestyle.com.description: boAt is the consumer electronics brand of Imagine Marketing Limited, a Mumbai company incorporated in 2013 whose founding members and promoters are Aman Gupta and Sameer Mehta. Its range covers true wireless earbuds, headphones, speakers, home audio and smartwatches, and has grown to include dashcams, projectors, trimmers and mobile accessories, sold through its website and its own shopping app. The company has published an updated draft red herring prospectus for a planned initial public offering. Dr Pawan Goenka chairs the board, and Mehta serves as an executive director.
boat-lifestyle.com.status: Active. Preparing an IPO (updated draft red herring prospectus published)

bolt.eu.name: Bolt
bolt.eu.description: Bolt was founded in Tallinn in 2013 by Markus Villig, who started it at 19, and it now operates in more than 50 countries. Its app covers ride-hailing, scooter and e-bike rental, car-sharing through Bolt Drive, and food and grocery delivery through Bolt Food and Bolt Market. The company reports over 200 million customers and about 4.5 million drivers, couriers and merchants working with it. In 2025 it bought the Copenhagen ride-hailing firm Viggo, its first acquisition, and it has signed autonomous vehicle partnerships with Stellantis, Lucid and Pony.ai.

brainly.com.name: Brainly
brainly.com.markets: US, Europe, Asia and Latin America
brainly.com.description: Brainly was started in Poland in 2009 by Michał Borkowski, Łukasz Haluch and Tomasz Kraus, and later opened a New York office alongside its original Polish base. Students post questions from their school subjects and get answers from other users, while the company's AI Learning Companion adds homework help, test preparation and tutoring. A paid tier, Brainly+, gives access to extra features. The service is used by students, parents and teachers in the United States, Europe, Asia and Latin America, and Borkowski remains chief executive.

brex.com.name: Brex
brex.com.description: Henrique Dubugras and Pedro Franceschi founded Brex in San Francisco in 2017 after going through Y Combinator. It sells corporate cards, business banking, expense and spend management software and real-time payments, and uses AI agents to automate expense and accounting work. Capital One completed its purchase of Brex in April 2026 for $5.15 billion in stock and cash, and Franceschi stayed on as chief executive. The business still operates under the Brex name within Capital One.
brex.com.status: Acquired by Capital One in April 2026

brightermonday.co.ke.name: BrighterMonday
brightermonday.co.ke.ownership: Subsidiary of The African Talent Company
products: CV review and AI career tool
brightermonday.co.ke.description: BrighterMonday was set up in Nairobi in 2006 and is now part of The African Talent Company, a pan-African group owned jointly by the Swiss media company Ringier and the Australian-listed jobs marketplace SEEK. Alongside vacancy listings and job alerts, it sells employers executive search, its Pro Recruit hiring service, HR outsourcing and staff training. Job seekers can use CV reviews, skills assessments and short courses. Sister sites in the same group include BrighterMonday Uganda and Jobberman in Nigeria and Ghana.

brilliant.org.name: Brilliant
brilliant.org.description: Brilliant teaches maths and coding through short interactive lessons in which learners solve problems as they go, on the web and in iOS and Android apps. Sue Khim launched the site in 2012, and it is run by Brilliant Worldwide, Inc. Its maths track starts with algebra and is adding geometry, probability and calculus, while its coding track covers Python and computer science. The team of about 60 works in a hybrid set-up around hubs in San Francisco and New York, and the company says it has hundreds of thousands of paid subscribers.

bsky.app.name: Bluesky
bsky.app.description: Bluesky Social PBC runs the Bluesky app on the web, iOS and Android, where people post short updates and pick which feeds they read. The project began at Twitter in 2019 under Jack Dorsey and became an independent public benefit corporation in 2021, led by Jay Graber. Graber stepped down as chief executive in March 2026 to become chief innovation officer and board chair, and Toni Schneider, the founding CEO of Automattic, was made permanent CEO that July. The company has no official headquarters and says it passed 44 million users in May 2026.

btcmarkets.net.name: BTC Markets
btcmarkets.net.description: BTC Markets runs a cryptocurrency exchange for Australian customers, with trading in Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Litecoin and other digital assets. It began operating in 2013 and works from Melbourne. The exchange serves individual traders, institutions and self-managed super funds, and added a mobile trading app in 2022. It reports more than 325,000 Australian traders and over AU$23 billion in total trade volume, and a sister company was granted an Australian Financial Services Licence in 2022.

bunq.com.name: bunq
bunq.com.description: bunq is an Amsterdam bank that runs entirely through its app and holds a European banking licence, which it received in September 2014. Ali Niknam founded the company in 2012 and still leads it as chief executive. The public app launched in November 2015 and the bank opened to customers across all EU markets in October 2019. It says it serves more than 22 million users, and it owns the group expense app tricount.

busuu.com.name: Busuu
busuu.com.description: Busuu was started in 2008 by Bernhard Niesner and Adrian Hilti, who met at IE Business School in Spain, and is based in London. Its courses cover about a dozen languages and mix short lessons, video clips and quizzes with AI speaking practice and corrections from native speakers. It reports over 120 million registered users and sells a corporate programme, Busuu for Business, to more than 600 organisations. The US education company Chegg bought Busuu for about US$436 million, with the deal completing in January 2022.

bybit.com.name: Bybit
bybit.com.description: Bybit operates a cryptocurrency exchange offering spot trading alongside perpetual contracts, futures and options. Ben Zhou founded it in 2018 in Singapore, and the company later moved its headquarters to Dubai. It says it has more than 80 million users worldwide. In the UAE it holds a full virtual asset platform operator licence from the Securities and Commodities Authority, and in October 2026 its Dubai entity received a VARA licence for spot exchange services.

cabify.com.name: Cabify
cabify.com.description: Cabify was founded in Madrid in 2011 by Juan de Antonio, who remains chief executive. It runs a ride-hailing app in more than 40 cities across Spain, Chile, Argentina, Peru, Colombia and Uruguay. Besides private rides it sells a corporate travel service for companies, a delivery and logistics arm and in-car advertising. The company reported revenue of about US$950 million for 2025.

calm.com.name: Calm
calm.com.description: Calm was started around 2012 by Michael Acton Smith and Alex Tew, and its app has passed 180 million downloads. Its library includes Sleep Stories, and it sells subscriptions monthly, yearly or as a one-off lifetime purchase. Calm Business supplies the app to employers, and Calm Health offers a clinical mental health programme through health plans and employers. The company works remote-first and hires staff across the UK and the US.

cambly.com.name: Cambly
cambly.com.description: Cambly was set up by Sameer Shariff and Kevin Law, two former Google employees, and went through the Y Combinator programme in San Francisco. Learners book video calls with English tutors on demand or follow structured courses in business English, grammar and exam preparation. Alongside one-to-one lessons it runs Cambly Kids for children, small group classes launched in 2022 and a corporate programme for companies. The platform takes students from more than 150 countries.

canonical.com.name: Canonical
canonical.com.description: Canonical was founded and funded in 2004 by Mark Shuttleworth to publish Ubuntu, the Linux distribution used on desktops, servers, cloud machines and devices. Revenue comes from Ubuntu Pro subscriptions, which add security maintenance and support, and from managed services for open source infrastructure such as OpenStack, Kubernetes, Ceph and databases. Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, released in April 2026, is the eleventh long-term supported version. The group is registered in London.

cardekho.com.name: CarDekho
cardekho.com.markets: India, plus Philippines, Malaysia and UAE through group sites
cardekho.com.description: CarDekho went live in 2008 and was started by Amit Jain and Anurag Jain in Jaipur. It is the main site of CarDekho Group, which also runs BikeDekho, ZigWheels, the vehicle loan platform Rupyy and car subscription brands Revv and Carrum, and holds a stake in InsuranceDekho. The group runs ZigWheels portals in the Philippines, Malaysia and the UAE. It reported consolidated operating revenue of ₹2,795 crore for FY25, and in July 2026 it was reported to be preparing draft papers for an Indian stock market listing.

careem.com.name: Careem
careem.com.description: Careem launched in Dubai in July 2012, founded by Mudassir Sheikha and Magnus Olsson, with Abdullah Elyas joining as a third co-founder in 2013. Its app combines ride-hailing with food ordering, Quik grocery delivery, the Careem Pay wallet and a Plus membership, and it says it has served more than 50 million customers. Uber bought Careem in 2019 and still owns the ride-hailing business, while the app and its other services sit in Careem Technologies. In June 2026 e& agreed to sell Uber a 12.5% stake in Careem Technologies, a deal that would give Uber control of that company.

carousell.com.name: Carousell
carousell.com.markets: Seven markets across Southeast Asia and Hong Kong
carousell.com.description: Carousell was launched in Singapore in August 2012 by Quek Siu Rui, Lucas Ngoo and Marcus Tan, who came up with the idea while studying at the National University of Singapore. The group now runs classifieds and resale businesses in seven markets, including Mudah.my in Malaysia, Cho Tot in Vietnam, the car platform OneShift, REFASH for second-hand fashion and Laku6 for used phones. It also operates physical resale stores in Singapore, Hong Kong, Malaysia and Indonesia. For FY25 it reported revenue of US$141 million and its first EBITDA profit.

cars24.com.name: CARS24
products: Car Info and Vehicle Info apps
cars24.com.description: CARS24 was founded in 2015 by Vikram Chopra, Mehul Agrawal, Ruchit Agarwal and Gajendra Jangid, and Chopra leads it as chief executive. It buys and sells used cars after inspection and adds loans, warranties and paperwork services such as registration transfers. Outside India it trades in Australia and the UAE. For FY26 it reported adjusted net revenue of ₹1,411 crore and ₹3,220 crore in loans disbursed, and its chief executive has said the company plans to list on Indian stock exchanges.

cashfree.com.name: Cashfree Payments
cashfree.com.markets: India, with cross-border collections and payouts
cashfree.com.description: Cashfree Payments was founded in 2015 by Akash Sinha and Reeju Datta and works from a headquarters in Bengaluru. It holds RBI authorisation as a payment aggregator for domestic and cross-border payments and as a prepaid payment instrument issuer. Its products cover online collections through more than 100 payment methods, bulk payouts, recurring payments, escrow and SecureID, a set of identity and KYC verification APIs. The company says it serves over one million businesses and processes about US$80 billion in transactions a year, and its investors include SBI, Apis Partners and KRAFTON.

casper.com.name: Casper
casper.com.description: Casper was founded in New York in 2014 by Philip Krim, Neil Parikh, Jeff Chapin, Gabe Flateman and Luke Sherwin, and began by selling a single mattress online. It listed on the New York Stock Exchange in early 2020 and was taken private by Durational Capital Management in 2022. In 2023 it sold its Canadian business to Sleep Country. Since late 2024 it has been a subsidiary of Carpenter Co., a polyurethane foam manufacturer based in Richmond, Virginia.

celonis.com.name: Celonis
celonis.com.description: Celonis was started in Munich in 2011 by a group of students including Alexander Rinke, now co-chief executive, and has dual headquarters in Munich and New York, with more than 20 offices in total. Its software reads event data from systems such as ERP and CRM tools to build a live model of how processes like order handling, invoicing and procurement actually run. The main product is the Celonis Process Intelligence Platform, which pairs process mining with AI, and the company added decision intelligence through its purchase of Ikigai Labs. It reports more than 3,000 employees.

checkout.com.name: Checkout.com
checkout.com.description: Checkout.com gives online merchants one platform for accepting cards and local payment methods, issuing cards, sending payouts, screening for fraud, verifying identities and managing treasury and FX. Founder and chief executive Guillaume Pousaz leads the company from London, and it employs about 2,000 people, with hubs added in San Francisco, Atlanta and São Paulo. It handled more than $300 billion in payment volume in 2025 and reported EBITDA profitability for the full year. Merchants using it include eBay, Vinted, Pinterest and ASOS.

chobani.com.name: Chobani
chobani.com.description: Hamdi Ulukaya founded Chobani in 2005 by buying a single yogurt plant in New Berlin, New York, and still runs it as chief executive from Chobani House in New York City. Besides Greek yogurt it sells high-protein milk, oat milk, coffee creamers and La Colombe canned coffee, made at plants in New York, Idaho and Michigan, and a new dairy plant is being built in Rome, New York. The company raised $650 million in October 2025 and expected net sales of $3.8 billion that year. In 2026 it bought a former Keurig Dr Pepper site in Allentown, Pennsylvania.

classdojo.com.name: ClassDojo
classdojo.com.description: ClassDojo was started in 2011 by Sam Chaudhary and Liam Don and is run from San Francisco by ClassDojo, Inc. Teachers use it to post classroom updates and message families, with messages translated into more than 190 languages, and the company says it is used in 95% of US schools. The core app is free, and families can pay for a ClassDojo Plus subscription. Other products include Dojo Islands, Dojo Tutor and paid tutoring in maths, reading and English as a second language, while ClassDojo for Districts adds districtwide messaging at no extra cost.

cleartrip.com.name: Cleartrip
cleartrip.com.description: Stuart Crighton, Hrush Bhatt and Matthew Spacie founded Cleartrip in 2006, and the business expanded into the Middle East in the 2010s, buying the Saudi travel site FlyIn in 2018. Flipkart bought all of Cleartrip in 2021 and kept it as a separate company. Through its website and app it sells flights, hotels, train and bus tickets and local activities. For the year to March 2026 it reported operating revenue of ₹198.3 crore, up about 21% on the previous year.

codecademy.com.name: Codecademy
codecademy.com.description: Zach Sims and his co-founder Ryan Bubinski started Codecademy in New York in August 2011, and Skillsoft, which is listed on the New York Stock Exchange, completed its purchase of the company in April 2022. Learners write and run code in the browser and can follow career paths built around projects, code challenges and interview preparation. The company also offers professional certification, bootcamps, workshops and coaching. Paid plans are sold to individuals, students and businesses, and the office is at 600 Broadway in Manhattan.

coindcx.com.name: CoinDCX
coindcx.com.description: Sumit Gupta and Neeraj Khandelwal founded CoinDCX in Mumbai in 2018, and in 2021 it became the first Indian crypto company valued at over $1 billion. The exchange lists more than 500 crypto assets across over 200 trading pairs for retail and institutional customers, and says it has more than 20 million users. It entered the Middle East in 2024 by buying the Dubai exchange BitOasis. CoinDCX sits within DCX Group alongside CoinDCX Ventures and the Web3 wallet Okto, and Coinbase took a minority stake in late 2025 at a $2.45 billion valuation.

coinone.co.kr.name: Coinone
products: Stock investment tab with Korea Investment & Securities
coinone.co.kr.description: Cha Myung-hoon founded Coinone in February 2014 and is once again its sole chief executive, after the company ended a brief co-CEO arrangement in March 2026. Customers trade digital assets against the Korean won through its website and mobile app. In 2026 Korea Investment & Securities and OKX Ventures each took a 20% stake for about $53 million apiece, leaving Cha with 30.36% and Com2uS Holdings with 24.54%. Since July 2026 the app has included a stock investment tab linked to Korea Investment & Securities' trading system.

coinspot.com.au.name: CoinSpot
coinspot.com.au.description: CoinSpot was set up near Melbourne in 2013 by Russell Wilson, its majority shareholder. It lists more than 460 digital currencies and says it has over 3 million customers, who can use instant buy and swap, coin bundles, over-the-counter trading, multicoin wallets and a CoinSpot Mastercard. It also offers accounts for self-managed super funds. CoinSpot has been registered with AUSTRAC as a virtual asset service provider since May 2018, and as of April 2026 it also holds an Australian Financial Services Licence regulated by ASIC.

coursehero.com.name: Course Hero
coursehero.com.description: Andrew Grauer co-founded Course Hero in a college dorm room in 2006, and in December 2022 the business reorganised under a new parent company, Learneo, which Grauer leads as chief executive. The site holds more than 30 million course-specific study resources contributed by students and educators, alongside practice problems, study guides, videos, class notes and step-by-step explanations. Course Hero also runs a Faculty Club for educators and monthly scholarships for students. Learneo's other brands include QuillBot, Scribbr, LitCharts, CliffsNotes and Symbolab.

cred.club.name: CRED
cred.club.description: Kunal Shah started CRED in Bengaluru in 2018 as a credit card bill payment app open only to people with high credit scores. Members can also make UPI payments, track their credit score and card spending, and redeem rewards on shopping and travel, and the company says about 1.7 crore members use its products each month. In June 2026 Meta agreed to lead a Rs 8,550 crore Series H round that values CRED at about Rs 43,239 crore. Shah stepped down as chief executive to run WhatsApp, and Miten Sampat became interim CEO.

crypto.com.name: Crypto.com
crypto.com.description: Crypto.com was founded in 2016 and is headquartered in Singapore, with co-founder Kris Marszalek as chief executive alongside co-founders Rafael Melo and Bobby Bao. It says it serves 150 million users in 90 countries through its main app, which covers buying, selling and staking crypto, tokenised stocks and prediction markets, while a separate exchange serves advanced traders. It also issues Visa prepaid cards, offers the Onchain wallet and is behind the Cronos blockchain. The company lists licences or registrations in markets including the United States, the UK, the EEA under MiCA, Singapore and Dubai.

cuemath.com.name: Cuemath
cuemath.com.description: Manan Khurma, an IIT Delhi graduate, started Cuemath in 2013 by teaching maths from his home in Delhi, and he still runs it as founder and chief executive. It now teaches live one-to-one online maths classes to school students in more than 80 countries through a pool of over 4,000 tutors. Courses run from the early grades up to AP level, alongside preparation for tests such as the SAT, MAP and AMC 8 and summer maths programmes. The company has an office in Gurugram and a US office, under CueLearn Inc, in Dover, Delaware, and says it is backed by Google and Sequoia Capital.

curve.com.name: Curve
products: Curve Pay X, Pro and Pro+ plans
Go Back in Time card switching
curve.com.description: Curve runs a payments app and card for customers in the UK and Europe, operating through Curve UK Limited in London and Curve Europe UAB in Vilnius. Users link the bank cards they already hold and can move a past purchase onto a different card, earn cashback and avoid some foreign exchange fees on spending abroad. Plans range from the free Curve Pay tier to the paid Pay X, Pay Pro and Pay Pro+ subscriptions. Lloyds Banking Group agreed to buy the company in November 2025 and completed the purchase in May 2026.
curve.com.status: Acquired by Lloyds Banking Group in May 2026

darktrace.com.name: Darktrace
darktrace.com.description: Darktrace develops cybersecurity software that learns the normal behaviour of an organisation's users and devices and flags or interrupts activity that departs from it. Its ActiveAI Security Platform covers email, networks and cloud environments as well as staff use of AI tools, and the company also sells managed security services. It started in Cambridge in 2013, has more than 2,300 staff and says it works with about 10,000 customers in 110 countries. The US private equity firm Thoma Bravo bought Darktrace for $5.3 billion in October 2024, ending its listing on the London Stock Exchange.
darktrace.com.status: Taken private by Thoma Bravo in October 2024

darwinbox.com.name: Darwinbox
darwinbox.com.description: Darwinbox builds human capital management software for large employers, covering recruitment, onboarding, core HR, payroll, attendance, performance reviews and employee self-service on mobile. Chaitanya Peddi, Jayant Paleti and Rohit Chennamaneni founded it in Hyderabad in 2015. It now sells to more than 1,000 enterprises that together run about 4 million employees on the platform across 130 countries. Its backers include Partners Group, KKR, Salesforce Ventures and Teachers' Venture Growth, which invested US$40 million in 2025, and the platform supports the Model Context Protocol so AI agents can work with its HR data.

datacamp.com.name: DataCamp
datacamp.com.description: DataCamp teaches data science, AI and programming in the browser, with short video lessons followed by coding exercises that learners complete on the page. Courses cover Python, R, SQL and machine learning, and learners can follow career tracks, sit certifications or analyse data in DataLab, its AI-assisted notebook. The company says 21 million people have signed up, and it sells team plans to employers alongside a classroom programme for schools and universities. It was launched in Belgium by Jonathan Cornelissen, Dieter De Mesmaeker and Martijn Theuwissen and now has offices in New York, Leuven and London.

deel.com.name: Deel
deel.com.description: Deel lets companies hire, pay and manage staff in other countries without opening local entities, either by acting as employer of record or by handling contractor agreements and payroll for them. Alex Bouaziz and Shuo Wang started the company in 2019, and it says it now works with more than 40,000 businesses across 150 countries. Its range has grown to cover HR records, benefits, device management, immigration support and a US PEO service. A US$300 million Series E in October 2025 valued Deel at US$17.3 billion, and its own staff of over 4,000 work remotely from more than 100 countries.

degiro.com.name: DEGIRO
degiro.com.description: DEGIRO started in 2008 as a broker for professional investors and opened its online service to private investors in the Netherlands in September 2013. It offers execution-only trading in shares, ETFs, bonds, options and futures on around 50 exchanges in Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific, and says it has more than 3 million clients. The German broker flatex bought DEGIRO in 2020. The business now trades as the Amsterdam-based Dutch branch of flatexDEGIRO Bank SE, which is supervised by BaFin in Germany and by the AFM and DNB in the Netherlands.

depop.com.name: Depop
depop.com.description: Depop began in 2011 at the H-Farm incubator near Venice, where Simon Beckerman built the first version of the app, and moved its base to London in 2012. Sellers run shop profiles and list items with photos, and its audience is young, with nearly 90% of its roughly 7 million active buyers aged under 34 at the end of 2025. It also had more than 3 million active sellers and handles around US$1 billion in gross merchandise sales a year. Etsy bought Depop in 2021, and eBay acquired it from Etsy for about US$1.2 billion in July 2026, keeping the brand and app separate.
depop.com.status: Acquired by eBay from Etsy in July 2026

dhgate.com.name: DHgate
dhgate.com.description: DHgate runs a cross-border marketplace where Chinese manufacturers and traders sell goods in small wholesale lots or single units to buyers abroad, in categories from electronics and clothing to home goods. Diane Wang founded the business in Beijing in August 2004, and the website went live in 2005. It lists more than 34 million products from over 2.5 million registered suppliers and reports nearly 60 million registered buyers in 225 countries and regions. The company was reorganised as DHgate Group in 2022, and its app reached second place on the US App Store in April 2025.

discord.com.name: Discord
discord.com.description: Discord launched in May 2015 as a voice and text chat app for people playing games together, built by Jason Citron and Stanislav Vishnevskiy after running their own games studio. Users join invite-based servers organised into channels, and can hold group calls, stream their screens and play shared activities. The basic service is free, with revenue from the Nitro subscription, server boosts and sponsored Quests, and it reported more than 90 million daily active users in late 2025. Humam Sakhnini became chief executive in April 2025, and the company filed confidentially for a US listing in January 2026 but remains private.

docker.com.name: Docker
docker.com.description: Docker, Inc. sells the commercial tools built around Docker, the open source container technology that packages an application with its dependencies so it runs the same way on any machine. The company began as the platform-as-a-service provider dotCloud and took the Docker name in 2013, when founder Solomon Hykes refocused it on containers. Its main products are Docker Desktop for developers' computers, the Docker Hub image registry, Docker Scout and Docker Hardened Images for supply chain security, and newer tools for running AI agents and models. The Palo Alto company says more than 20 million developers use its software.

doctolib.fr.name: Doctolib
doctolib.fr.markets: France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and the UK
doctolib.fr.description: Doctolib sells practice management and scheduling software to doctors, dentists and other health professionals, and runs a free website and app where patients book appointments and video consultations. Stanislas Niox-Chateau and a small team launched it in France in 2013, and it now operates in France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom. The company says it serves 520,000 health professionals and 90 million patients. In 2026 it entered the UK by buying Medicus, a supplier of GP electronic patient records, and Nvidia took a minority stake in October 2026 to support its AI work for clinicians and patients.

dubizzle.com.name: dubizzle
dubizzle.com.description: dubizzle has run online classifieds in Dubai since 2005 and now carries listings from Abu Dhabi, Sharjah and the other emirates, with sections for property sales and rentals, motors, jobs and general goods. It was started by Sim Whatley and JC Butler, who ran it as joint chief executives. The site now belongs to Dubizzle Group, a Dubai company backed by Prosus that also owns Bayut, Hatla2ee and Property Monitor and has more than 2,600 staff across the region. The group planned a Dubai Financial Market listing in October 2025 but postponed it.

duckduckgo.com.name: DuckDuckGo
duckduckgo.com.description: DuckDuckGo runs a search engine and builds its own web browser for Mac, Windows, iOS and Android, along with Email Protection, the Duck.ai chat service and a paid subscription that bundles a VPN, personal information removal and identity theft restoration. Gabriel Weinberg started the company in 2008 from his basement in Pennsylvania, and it has stayed independent since then. Its team of about 335 people works remotely from more than 15 countries. The company reports around 3 billion searches a month on its engine.

ebanx.com.name: EBANX
products: Local payment methods such as Pix
ebanx.com.description: EBANX processes payments for international merchants that sell to consumers in emerging markets, connecting them through one integration to local methods such as Brazil's Pix instant transfers, cash vouchers and instalment plans. Its services also include payouts and recurring billing. The company was started in Curitiba, Brazil, in 2012 by Alphonse Voigt, Wagner Ruiz and João Del Valle and now has more than 700 staff based in 16 countries. It covers most of Latin America and parts of Africa and Asia, and opened an Asia-Pacific base in Singapore in March 2026.

emma-sleep.com.name: Emma
emma-sleep.com.description: Emma sells mattresses, pillows, bedding and bed frames, mostly through its own websites, and offers a 100-night trial and a ten-year guarantee on its mattresses. Dennis Schmoltzi and Manuel Müller started the business in Frankfurt in 2013, and the Emma brand has been on sale since 2015. The company trades in more than 25 markets, runs over 25 shops in Europe and has more than 900 staff working from offices in Frankfurt, Manila, Lisbon and Mexico City. It says it has sold to more than 5 million customers.

flexport.com.name: Flexport
flexport.com.description: Flexport books and manages international freight for importers and exporters and files their customs entries as a licensed broker, with bookings, documents and tracking handled in its own software. It also runs warehousing and fulfilment for online and wholesale orders and offers trade finance and cargo insurance. Ryan Petersen started the company in San Francisco in 2013, and it now has about 60 offices and warehouses and a network covering 135 countries. Time magazine included its Customs Technology Suite in its 2026 inventions list.

flixbus.com.name: FlixBus
flixbus.com.description: FlixBus is the coach brand of Flix SE, a Munich company founded in 2011 by André Schwämmlein, Daniel Krauss and Jochen Engert. Alongside FlixBus, Flix runs FlixTrain rail services, Greyhound in North America and Kâmil Koç in Türkiye, and its network reaches about 8,700 destinations in 45 countries. The group has more than 5,500 staff and says it has carried over 500 million passengers since launch. The investment firm EQT and Kühne Holding agreed in 2024 to buy a 35% stake in the company.

free-now.com.name: Freenow
free-now.com.description: Freenow runs a ride app that books licensed taxis and private hire cars, with eScooters and eBikes also offered in some cities and a business travel service for companies. The service has operated since 2009 and now covers more than 180 cities in the UK, Ireland, Germany, Spain, Italy, France, Greece, Poland and Austria, including pickups at around 50 airports. Lyft, the US ride-hailing company, completed its purchase of Freenow on 31 July 2025, and the app now trades as Freenow by Lyft.

freetrade.io.name: Freetrade
freetrade.io.description: Freetrade runs a mobile and web investing platform for UK customers, offering stocks and shares ISAs, Junior ISAs, self-invested personal pensions and general accounts on Basic, Standard or Plus plans. Customers can buy UK, US and European shares, ETFs, funds, gilts and Treasury bills. Adam Dodds, Viktor Nebehaj and Davide Fioranelli founded the company in London in 2016, and it opened to customers in 2018 with commission-free share dealing. Freetrade Limited is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority and has been owned by IG Group since April 2025.
freetrade.io.status: Acquired by IG Group in April 2025

getyourguide.com.name: GetYourGuide
getyourguide.com.description: GetYourGuide sells tickets and bookings for tours, museums, attractions and day trips from about 50,000 supply partners, with some 200,000 experiences listed in more than 18,000 cities. The business began as a student project at ETH Zurich and is now based in Berlin, with a second office in Zurich. Its founders include Johannes Reck, who is chief executive, and Tao Tao, the chief operating officer. Travellers booked 10 million experiences through the platform in the third quarter of 2025, and the company reported a profit on an adjusted EBITDA basis.

glossier.com.name: Glossier
glossier.com.description: Glossier sells make-up, skincare and fragrance through its own website, its shops and Sephora, which has stocked the brand in the US and Canada since 2023. Emily Weiss launched Glossier in 2014 and handed the chief executive role to Kyle Leahy in 2022. Colin Walsh now leads the company, and in March 2026 it said it would close nine of its 12 shops over about two and a half years, keeping flagships in New York, Los Angeles and London. It is also trimming its range to focus on core products and the Glossier You fragrance line.

glovoapp.com.name: Glovo
glovoapp.com.markets: 21 countries in Europe, Central Asia and Africa
glovoapp.com.description: Glovo was founded in Barcelona in 2015 by Oscar Pierre and Sacha Michaud and has been part of the German group Delivery Hero since 2022. Its app connects customers with restaurants, supermarkets and other local shops, and with the couriers who carry their orders, in 21 countries across Europe, Central Asia and Africa. The company employs around 3,000 people. Under Uber's pending takeover of Delivery Hero, announced in July 2026, Glovo's businesses in Spain, Portugal, Poland, Romania and Moldova are due to be sold to the investment firm SSW Partners, with completion expected in the second half of 2027.
glovoapp.com.status: Active. Parent Delivery Hero is subject to a pending takeover by Uber, expected to close in the second half of 2027

gocardless.com.name: GoCardless
gocardless.com.description: GoCardless collects payments by bank debit and open banking for businesses that bill customers regularly or once, such as subscriptions, memberships, instalments and invoices. Its tools include Success+ for retrying failed payments, Protect+ for fraud screening and more than 350 integrations with accounting and billing software. The London company is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority, has offices in Australia, France, Latvia and the United States, and says more than 100,000 businesses use it. Mollie completed its acquisition of GoCardless on 1 September 2026, and co-founder Hiroki Takeuchi continues to run the business.
gocardless.com.status: Acquired by Mollie in September 2026; trades as GoCardless, a Mollie company

gonoise.com.name: Noise
gonoise.com.description: Noise was founded in 2014 by Gaurav Khatri, its chief executive, and Amit Khatri, and is run by Gurugram-based Nexxbase Marketing. The company began by selling smartphone cases and covers before moving into wearables and audio in 2018. It sells through its own website and the large Indian e-commerce platforms. Bose has invested twice, $10 million in December 2023 and $20 million in 2025, and Noise has released audio products with Sound by Bose. For FY25 it reported revenue of ₹1,065.5 crore and a small net profit.

gopuff.com.name: Gopuff
gopuff.com.description: Gopuff was founded in 2013 by Yakir Gola and Rafael Ilishayev while they were students at Drexel University in Philadelphia, where the company is still based. It runs more than 400 of its own micro-fulfilment centres in the United States and the UK, stocking over 5,000 products for delivery in as little as 15 minutes. Members of its paid FAM scheme get lower prices on many items. In 2026 it added Go, an AI shopping feature in its app built with SpaceXAI, after raising $250 million in a round led by Eldridge Industries in late 2025.

gostudent.org.name: GoStudent
gostudent.org.description: GoStudent sells online one-to-one tutoring for school pupils in subjects ranging from maths and the sciences to languages, with UK lessons pitched from Key Stage 1 up to A levels. Felix Ohswald and Gregor Müller began it as a WhatsApp homework chat in 2015 and launched the app in 2016, and the company is registered in Vienna. It runs local sites in ten European countries, including the UK, Germany, France, Spain and Italy. GoStudent has also bought the AI revision platform Seneca Learning, the in-person tutoring company Studienkreis and the tutoring marketplace Tus Media.

grammarly.com.name: Grammarly
grammarly.com.description: Grammarly makes an AI writing assistant that suggests corrections and rewrites as people type in more than a million apps and websites, through browser extensions, desktop apps for Windows and Mac, mobile keyboards and add-ins for Microsoft Office and Google Docs. Max Lytvyn, Alex Shevchenko and Dmytro Lider founded the company in 2009, and it sells Free, Pro and Education plans. In 2025 it bought the document tool Coda and the email app Superhuman Mail. In October 2025 the company took the Superhuman name and kept Grammarly as a product in its suite, which reports more than 40 million daily users.
grammarly.com.status: Company renamed Superhuman in October 2025; Grammarly continues as a product

greythr.com.name: greytHR
greythr.com.markets: India, the Gulf states and 30+ countries
greythr.com.description: greytHR, made by Bengaluru-based Greytip Software, is an HR and payroll system used mainly by small and mid-sized employers in India and the Gulf states. Its modules cover payroll, leave, attendance, performance reviews, recruitment, expense claims and an employee self-service app, and it has added an AI assistant called NAVOS. The company says more than 34,000 businesses in over 30 countries use it. In 2024 Apax Digital Fund II took a 52.1% stake in the business.

gulftalent.com.name: GulfTalent
gulftalent.com.description: GulfTalent runs a job portal for professional and managerial roles across the Gulf states and the wider Middle East. Job seekers can search vacancies, keep an online profile and sign up for email job alerts, while employers use the site to advertise openings and reach candidates. The company was founded in 2005, recruits its own staff in Dubai, and says about 10 million people and around 9,000 companies use the platform. It also publishes guides and research on hiring activity and job hunting in the region.

gusto.com.name: Gusto
gusto.com.description: Gusto sells payroll, benefits and HR software to small businesses across the US. Employers use it to run payroll, offer health and retirement benefits, hire and onboard staff, track hours and keep up with compliance. It started in 2011 as ZenPayroll, founded by Josh Reeves, Eddie Kim and Tomer London, and has headquarters in San Francisco and Denver. The company has about 3,000 employees and more than 500,000 business customers, and said in early 2026 that its revenue had passed $1 billion.

headspace.com.name: Headspace
headspace.com.description: Headspace began as a meditation app started in 2010 by Andy Puddicombe and Rich Pierson, and now combines guided meditation and sleep content with text-based coaching, licensed therapists and psychiatry. It merged with the teletherapy company Ginger in 2021, and much of its business comes from employers and health plans that offer it to staff and members, including as a replacement for a traditional employee assistance programme. The company says its app has been downloaded more than 105 million times. In September 2026 Headspace became part of Sword Health in an all-cash deal worth up to 300 million US dollars.
headspace.com.status: Acquired by Sword Health in September 2026

hmd.com.name: HMD
hmd.com.description: HMD, the trading name of HMD Global Oy, is a Finnish phone maker based in Espoo that took over the licence to sell Nokia-branded phones in 2016 after Microsoft left the phone business. It still sells phones under the Nokia licence alongside its own HMD-branded smartphones and feature phones, including repairable and family-focused models. A secure division makes devices such as the HMD Terra M for government and business users, and its Softlock platform lets retailers sell phones on credit with device-based locking. Jean-François Baril is chairman and chief executive.

hopper.com.name: Hopper
products: Price freeze and flexible booking add-ons
Travel booking technology for banks and partners
hopper.com.description: Hopper is a travel booking app whose main feature is price tracking that tells users whether to book now or wait. It was founded in Montreal in 2007 by former Expedia engineers including chief executive Frederic Lalonde and Joost Ouwerkerk, and spent several years building its price data before the app launched. Much of its revenue comes from booking commissions and paid add-ons such as price freezes and flexible cancellation. Hopper also licenses its booking technology to other companies, and RBC uses it to run the travel side of its Avion Rewards programme.

hostinger.com.name: Hostinger
hostinger.com.description: Hostinger sells web hosting, domains and website building tools to small businesses, freelancers and individuals. It started in Kaunas in 2004 as Hosting Media, a company bootstrapped by a group of young Lithuanian entrepreneurs, and is now based in Vilnius with more than 1,000 staff. Alongside shared, WordPress, VPS and cloud hosting, it offers an AI website builder, business email and a range of AI agent and automation tools such as self-hosted n8n. The company says more than five million businesses and creators in over 150 countries use its services.

hudabeauty.com.name: Huda Beauty
hudabeauty.com.description: Huda Beauty is a cosmetics brand started in Dubai in 2013 by the make-up artist and blogger Huda Kattan, whose first product was a range of false eyelashes. It now sells colour cosmetics and skincare through its own website and through retailers such as Sephora. TSG Consumer Partners held a minority stake from 2017 until June 2025, when Kattan bought back all outstanding shares and the brand returned to full independent ownership. Earlier in 2025 she sold her stake in the fragrance brand Kayali to her sister Mona Kattan, who runs it separately.

huel.com.name: Huel
huel.com.markets: UK, Europe and the United States
huel.com.description: Huel was set up by entrepreneur Julian Hearn and former NHS dietitian James Collier and began selling powdered complete meals in 2015. It now also makes ready-to-drink shakes, hot savoury meals, bars, greens powders and functional drinks, sold mainly direct to customers online, with a manufacturing site and warehouse in Milton Keynes. The UK is its largest market, followed by continental Europe and the United States, and revenue reached about £254 million in its tenth financial year. The French food group Danone completed its purchase of Huel in September 2026, with James McMaster as chief executive.

idealista.com.name: idealista
products: Property listings for sale and rent
idealista.com.description: idealista runs online property portals in Spain, Italy and Portugal, where private owners and estate agents advertise homes, offices, garages and rooms for sale or rent. It was founded in Madrid in 2000 by the brothers Jesús and Fernando Encinar with César Oteiza, and Jesús Encinar remains chief executive. The private equity firm Cinven bought a majority stake from EQT in a deal valuing the company at about €2.9 billion, with founders and management keeping a share. Besides listings it sells software and data services to agents and has bought smaller businesses such as the overseas buyers' portal Kyero.

immobiliare.it.name: Immobiliare.it
products: Property listings for sale and rent
Software and services for estate agents
immobiliare.it.description: Immobiliare.it runs one of Italy's main property listing sites, where estate agents, builders and private owners advertise homes and commercial premises for sale or rent. It was set up in 2005 by Silvio Pagliani and Andrea Piccioni, and Pagliani took over as chief executive in 2022. The company works from offices in Rome and Milan and heads a group of property portals in other countries, including Spitogatos in Greece, Immotop in Luxembourg, Nepremicnine.net in Slovenia and Indomio in Spain and the Balkans. It also runs the international site LuxuryEstate.com.

impossiblefoods.com.name: Impossible Foods
impossiblefoods.com.markets: United States, Canada, UK, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Hong Kong, Macau and UAE
impossiblefoods.com.description: Impossible Foods makes plant-based versions of beef, chicken and pork, sold in supermarkets and to restaurants. It grew out of work begun in 2009 by the Stanford biochemist Pat Brown and is based in Redwood City, California. Its best known product is the Impossible Burger, launched in 2016, which uses soy leghemoglobin, a protein made by fermentation, to give a meat-like flavour and colour. The products are sold in nine markets including the United States, Canada, the UK, Australia and Singapore. Since chief executive Peter McGuinness left in January 2026, a three-person executive team has run the company.

independentreserve.com.name: Independent Reserve
independentreserve.com.description: Independent Reserve is a Sydney-based cryptocurrency exchange founded in 2013 by Adrian Przelozny, Adam Tepper and Lasanka Perera. It lets individuals, companies, trusts and self-managed super funds buy and sell crypto in Australian, New Zealand and other currencies, and runs an OTC desk for larger trades. In Australia it is registered with AUSTRAC as a digital currency exchange, and in 2021 it became the first Australian exchange to receive a Major Payment Institution licence from the Monetary Authority of Singapore. The company says it has more than 550,000 clients.

indrive.com.name: inDrive
indrive.com.markets: Latin America, Africa, Asia and other regions, about 1,100 cities
indrive.com.description: inDrive runs a ride-hailing app built around fare negotiation, in which passengers name a price and nearby drivers accept it or make a counter-offer. Arsen Tomsky started the service in Yakutsk, Siberia, in 2013 and remains chief executive. It works mainly in Latin America, Africa, South and Central Asia and Southeast Asia, with Brazil, Colombia, India, Indonesia and Pakistan among its largest markets, and it says the app has been downloaded 400 million times. Besides city and intercity rides it offers courier deliveries and a financial services line called inDrive.Money, and employs close to 3,000 people across 28 offices.

instructure.com.name: Instructure
instructure.com.description: Instructure develops Canvas, a learning management system that schools, universities and employers use to run courses, set assignments and track grades online. The company was founded in 2008 and is based in Salt Lake City, Utah, with further offices in London and Quezon City. It also owns Mastery Connect for school assessment and Parchment, a service for sending academic transcripts and credentials. Instructure was listed on the New York Stock Exchange until November 2024, when the investment firm KKR, with Dragoneer, completed a 4.8 billion US dollar purchase and took it private. It says its tools reach about 200 million learners.
instructure.com.status: Active (taken private by KKR in November 2024)

internshala.com.name: Internshala
internshala.com.description: Internshala began in 2010 as a blog run by IIT Madras graduate Sarvesh Agrawal and launched its website in 2013, later adding an Android app in 2015. Based in Gurugram, it lists internships and fresher jobs posted by employers, and sells short online trainings and placement courses in subjects such as digital marketing, data science and full stack development. It reports more than 34 million registered users and around 450,000 employers. In February 2026 the edtech company upGrad agreed to acquire it in a mostly stock-swap deal, with Internshala kept as a separate brand under Agrawal.
internshala.com.status: Acquired by upGrad in 2026, operating as a separate brand

italki.com.name: italki
italki.com.description: italki is a marketplace where people book private video lessons with language teachers who set their own prices and timetables. It was founded in 2007 by Kevin Chen and Yongyue Jiang, is registered in Hong Kong as italki HK Limited, and has run its development work from Shanghai. Learners choose between professional teachers and community tutors, and pay per lesson or in packages. The site says it lists more than 20,000 teachers covering over 150 languages, with learners from more than 190 countries, and it also offers language level assessments.

iyzico.com.name: iyzico
iyzico.com.description: iyzico was founded in Istanbul in 2012 by Barbaros Özbugutu and Tahsin Işın and handles online and in-store card payments for Turkish businesses, from small sellers to marketplaces. Its merchant products include a virtual POS, payment links, subscriptions, mass payouts and fraud controls, while shoppers use the iyzico app and Pay with iyzico to store cards and pay. PayU, part of Prosus, bought the company in 2019, and in 2025 iyzico completed its purchase of the payments firm Paynet. It reports 185,000 merchant members and 7 million wallet users, and in March 2026 announced a move into Europe through a Dutch subsidiary.

jetbrains.com.name: JetBrains
jetbrains.com.description: JetBrains builds development environments and other tools for programmers, among them IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, Rider and CLion, plus team products such as TeamCity and YouTrack. It created the Kotlin language and now also sells AI coding tools, including the Junie agent. Sergey Dmitriev, Eugene Belyaev and Valentin Kipiatkov founded the company in Prague in February 2000. It is privately owned, has its headquarters in Amsterdam and 14 offices, and reports more than 2,600 staff and 12.5 million recurring active users.

jimdo.com.name: Jimdo
jimdo.com.description: Jimdo is a Hamburg website builder aimed at self-employed people and small businesses, with plans that cover websites, online shops, appointment booking, domains and marketing tools. Christian Springub, Fridtjof Detzner and Matthias Henze started it in 2007, and Henze is chief executive. The company is wholly owned by its founders and has about 230 staff. In 2025 it launched Companion, a set of AI tools for winning customers and handling enquiries, first in the US, UK, Ireland and the German-speaking countries.

jobberman.com.name: Jobberman
jobberman.com.parent: The African Talent Company (Ringier One Africa Media)
jobberman.com.ownership: Subsidiary of The African Talent Company
jobberman.com.description: Jobberman runs job sites in Nigeria and Ghana where candidates search vacancies, take skills assessments and use online learning, and where employers post listings or hire through paid recruitment services, including executive search. Opeyemi Awoyemi, Olalekan Olude and Ayodeji Adewunmi founded it in 2009, when Awoyemi was studying at Obafemi Awolowo University. One Africa Media took full ownership in 2015. Jobberman now sits within The African Talent Company, part of Ringier One Africa Media, alongside BrighterMonday in Kenya and Uganda, and its Nigerian office is in Lagos.

joinhandshake.com.name: Handshake
joinhandshake.com.description: Handshake runs a careers network that links university students and recent graduates with employers, working through university career centres that give their students access. Garrett Lord, Ben Christensen and Scott Ringwelski started the company in 2014, and it says more than 1,600 educational institutions and about one million employers now use it. It has also set up Handshake AI, which recruits people with specialist knowledge for AI training and evaluation work. The company has offices in San Francisco, New York, the UK and Bangalore.

kahoot.com.name: Kahoot!
kahoot.com.description: Kahoot! runs a quiz and learning platform used in schools, universities and companies, where a host builds questions that players answer live on their own devices or work through at their own pace. Morten Versvik, Johan Brand and Jamie Brooker founded it in Oslo in 2012, and it now has more than 600 staff in offices across 11 countries. The group also owns Clever, DragonBox and the language app Drops, among others. Kahoot! was listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange from 2021 until 2024, when Goldman Sachs Asset Management, General Atlantic, KIRKBI and the Kahoot! team took it private.
kahoot.com.status: Active. Delisted from the Oslo Stock Exchange in 2024 after a take-private deal

keka.com.name: Keka
keka.com.markets: India, US, Middle East and the Philippines
keka.com.description: Keka makes cloud HR and payroll software for small and mid-sized companies, covering payroll processing and statutory compliance, employee records, attendance and leave, recruitment, performance reviews, and timesheets and billing for project-based firms. Vijay Yalamanchili founded it in Hyderabad in 2015. In 2022 it raised $57 million from WestBridge Capital, reported at the time as the largest Series A round for an Indian SaaS company. Besides India, it sells in the US, the Gulf states and the Philippines and has an office in Texas.

klook.com.name: Klook
klook.com.description: Klook sells tickets and bookings for tours, attractions, activities and local transport through its website and app, mainly to travellers in Asia Pacific. Ethan Lin, Eric Gnock Fah and Bernie Xiong founded it in Hong Kong in 2014, and Lin is chief executive. Asia Pacific made up nearly 87% of its gross transaction value in 2024, a year in which gross bookings came to $2.5 billion. Klook filed to list on the New York Stock Exchange in November 2025 but withdrew the offering in October 2026 and remains privately held.
klook.com.status: Active. Withdrew its planned US IPO in October 2026

koho.ca.name: KOHO
koho.ca.description: KOHO is a Toronto-based financial technology company whose app combines a prepaid Mastercard spending account with high-interest savings, cash back, credit building and credit score tools, cash advances and international money transfers. Its cards are issued by KOHO Financial Inc. Founder and chief executive Daniel Eberhard launched the service in 2014, and it now has more than 2.5 million Canadian users. In June 2026 KOHO raised C$130 million at a C$1.33 billion valuation, while its application for a federal bank licence was still awaiting approval.

konga.com.name: Konga
konga.com.description: Konga runs an online marketplace in Nigeria selling electronics, phones, fashion and household goods, backed by its own logistics arm for last-mile delivery. Sim Shagaya launched it in 2012. The Zinox Group bought Konga in 2018 from investors including Naspers and Kinnevik, and Nnamdi Ekeh is group chief executive. Alongside online shopping, the business runs KongaPay payments, Konga Health, Konga Travel and Tours, retail operations, a corporate sales unit and Konga TV and FM.

kraken.com.name: Kraken
kraken.com.description: Kraken runs a cryptocurrency exchange where individuals and institutions buy, sell and trade digital assets, with margin and perpetual futures trading, staking, an OTC desk, prime brokerage and the Kraken Pro platform for active traders. It also offers tokenised US shares through xStocks, and its related businesses include NinjaTrader and CF Benchmarks. Jesse Powell co-founded Kraken in 2011, and its parent company, Payward, reported 6.6 million funded accounts in the second quarter of 2026. Payward has filed confidentially for a US listing, which reports in September 2026 said was unlikely before the second quarter of 2027.

kucoin.com.name: KuCoin
kucoin.com.description: KuCoin runs a cryptocurrency exchange that lists more than 1,000 tokens and offers spot, futures and margin trading, automated trading bots, savings and staking products under KuCoin Earn, OTC trading and a KuCard payment card. Its first code was written in late 2013 and the platform launched in 2017. BC Wong became chief executive in 2025. KuCoin says it has 45 million users in more than 200 countries and regions, holds a MiCA licence for its EU entity and an AUSTRAC registration in Australia, and runs a regulated exchange in Thailand.

lalamove.com.name: Lalamove
lalamove.com.markets: 18 markets across Asia, Latin America and EMEA
lalamove.com.description: Lalamove is the international brand of Hong Kong-based Lalatech, which runs an app-based delivery platform matching businesses and individuals with independent drivers of motorcycles, vans and trucks. Chow Shing-yuk founded the business in Hong Kong in 2013 and is chairman and chief executive. Outside mainland China, where the group trades as Huolala, Lalamove lists 18 markets across Asia, Latin America and EMEA, including Japan, Brazil, Türkiye, the UAE and the UK. Across the group, about 2.1 million carriers and 21.3 million merchants used the platform each month on average in 2025.
lalamove.com.status: Active. Parent Lalatech filed an updated Hong Kong listing application in April 2026 and is not yet listed

ledger.com.name: Ledger
ledger.com.description: Ledger makes hardware signers, small devices that keep the private keys for crypto assets offline, including the Nano range, Flex, Stax and the newer Atom. Its Ledger Wallet app lets owners buy, swap and stake assets, and the company also sells Ledger Enterprise and multisig tools to institutions and a card for spending crypto. Ledger started in 2014 and is based in Paris, with more than 700 staff across eight offices, among them Vierzon, London, Portland and Singapore. It says it has sold over 8 million signers to clients in 180 countries.

li.me.name: Lime
li.me.description: Lime rents out dockless electric scooters and e-bikes that riders find and start through its app for short trips, in about 230 cities across 29 countries. Toby Sun and Brad Bao co-founded the business in 2017 and it is based in San Francisco, with Wayne Ting as chief executive. Its holding company, Neutron Holdings, listed on Nasdaq under the ticker LIME in July 2026, raising about $167 million at $25 a share. Uber holds a 24% stake, and Lime reported revenue of $886.7 million for 2025.
li.me.status: Active. Listed on Nasdaq in July 2026

luno.com.name: Luno
products: Crypto buying, selling and storage app
Crypto as a service for partners
luno.com.description: Luno runs a crypto investment app and exchange that started in South Africa in 2013 under the name BitX and is now headquartered in London. Digital Currency Group, the US crypto investment firm, bought the whole company in September 2020. Besides retail trading and staking, Luno offers white-label crypto services for partners, an over-the-counter desk with a cross-border settlement network, and Zaru, a rand-backed stablecoin launched in February 2026. In mid-2026 it narrowed its focus to core markets in Africa and South East Asia and stopped serving some other regions from 1 September 2026.

magoosh.com.name: Magoosh
magoosh.com.description: Magoosh was started in 2009 by students at the Haas School of Business at the University of California, Berkeley, and the company is still based in Berkeley, although it has worked fully remotely since March 2020. Its self-paced courses cover the GRE, GMAT, LSAT, MCAT, SAT, ACT, TOEFL, IELTS and Praxis, combining short video lessons with practice questions. Magoosh says more than 10 million students have used its material, with learners in 185 countries. It also sells test prep packages to high schools and colleges, and co-founder Bhavin Parikh is chief executive.

malt.com.name: Malt
malt.com.markets: Nine countries and regions in Europe and the Middle East
malt.com.description: Malt began in France in 2013 under the name Hopwork and took its current name as it expanded into other European countries. Companies use the platform to find, contract and pay freelance developers, designers, marketers, data specialists and consultants, with Malt handling the paperwork and payments between the two sides. In June 2026 it reported more than one million registered freelancers and over 100,000 client businesses, and said business volume on the platform passed 800 million euros in 2024. Its head office is in Paris, and clients it names include Schneider Electric, L'Oréal and Reckitt.

masterclass.com.name: MasterClass
masterclass.com.description: MasterClass launched in San Francisco in May 2015 with online classes recorded by well-known practitioners, from chefs and novelists to athletes and business founders. An annual membership gives unlimited access to a library of more than 200 instructors and classes. The company has since added MasterClass at Work, which sells training to employers, MasterClass On Call, which offers AI roleplays and real-time coaching, and certificate programmes developed with companies. Co-founder Aaron Rasmussen was the company's first chief technology officer and creative director.

medium.com.name: Medium
medium.com.description: Medium was launched in August 2012 by Twitter co-founder Evan Williams as a place where anyone could publish long-form writing. The site sells no advertising and is paid for by reader memberships, part of which goes to writers whose stories members read. Medium says more than 100 million people use it each month, and many companies, editors and writers run their own publications on it. Tony Stubblebine took over from Williams as chief executive in 2022.

memrise.com.name: Memrise
memrise.com.description: Memrise was founded in London in 2010 by memory champion Ed Cooke, Ben Whately and neuroscientist Greg Detre, and began as a vocabulary tool built on spaced repetition. The app now mixes word drills with short videos of native speakers, AI conversation practice, pronunciation tools and exam preparation for IELTS, GCSE, A-Level and IB with AI marking. The company says it has had more than 80 million learners in 189 countries and offers courses in 149 languages. It runs with a small team of around a dozen people.

mercadobitcoin.com.br.name: Mercado Bitcoin
mercadobitcoin.com.br.description: Mercado Bitcoin has run a cryptocurrency exchange in Brazil since 2013, letting customers buy and sell bitcoin, stablecoins and other digital assets in reais. It belongs to the holding company 2TM, whose chief executive Roberto Dagnoni also chairs and runs the exchange. In 2023 the Central Bank of Brazil authorised the group to operate as a payment institution issuing electronic money, which backs its MB Pay digital account. By July 2026 the platform had about 4.5 million users and had taken a R$100 million investment from Tether to expand into payments and tokenised investments.

mercury.com.name: Mercury
products: Working capital loans and venture debt
mercury.com.description: Mercury was set up in San Francisco in 2017 by three former colleagues from the ad network Heyzap and opened its first accounts in 2019. It is a financial technology company rather than a bank, and its deposit accounts are held at partner banks Choice Financial Group and Column N.A. Beyond checking and savings it offers cards, bill pay, invoicing, payroll, accounting software and lending, and says it serves more than 300,000 businesses. In April 2026 it won conditional approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to form Mercury Bank, N.A., which will be based in Utah.

mollie.com.name: Mollie
mollie.com.description: Mollie was started in Amsterdam in 2004 by Adriaan Mol and grew into a payments provider for European businesses of all sizes, from web shops to software platforms that embed payments. Mollie B.V. is licensed as an electronic money institution by De Nederlandsche Bank, and Mollie UK Ltd is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority. Alongside card and local payment methods it offers in-person terminals, recurring billing, business accounts and merchant financing. In September 2026 it completed its purchase of the UK direct debit company GoCardless, and the combined group serves more than 350,000 businesses in over 30 markets under chief executive Koen Köppen.

momo.vn.name: MoMo
momo.vn.legalName: Công ty Cổ phần Dịch vụ Di động Trực tuyến (M_Service)
momo.vn.description: MoMo is run by M_Service, a Ho Chi Minh City company set up in 2007 that launched the e-wallet three years later. Its payment intermediary services, including the e-wallet and payment gateway, are licensed by the State Bank of Vietnam, and the app links to more than 36 banks and the Visa, Mastercard and JCB networks. Beyond payments it offers a pay-later wallet, small loans, insurance and ticket booking. Co-founder and chief executive Nguyen Manh Tuong leads a business with more than 30 million users.

monzo.com.name: Monzo
monzo.com.description: Monzo Bank was started in London in 2015 and is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the FCA and PRA. It says it serves more than 16 million personal and business customers, with offices in London and Cardiff. Alongside everyday accounts it sells savings, ISAs, investments, pensions, credit and paid subscription plans. In the year to March 2026 revenue rose 39% to £1.7bn, and group chief executive Diana Layfield has said the bank is preparing to launch in Europe.

mubi.com.name: MUBI
