mubi.com.description: MUBI was founded by Efe Çakarel in 2007 under the name The Auteurs and is based in London, with around 400 staff across about 15 offices. The service is available in 190 countries, and the MUBI GO plan adds a weekly cinema ticket in some cities. It also releases films in cinemas, finances productions and owns the sales and production company The Match Factory, bought in 2022. Films it has acquired for release include The Substance, picked up in 2024.

mygreatlearning.com.name: Great Learning
mygreatlearning.com.legalName: Great Learning Education Services Pvt Ltd
mygreatlearning.com.description: Great Learning runs online and blended professional programmes in data science, artificial intelligence, cloud computing and management, many of them delivered with university and business school partners. Its Great Learning Academy offers short self-paced courses at no charge. The company was founded in 2013 by Mohan Lakhamraju, Arjun Nair and Hari Krishnan Nair and is based in Bengaluru. BYJU'S bought it in 2021, but the deal was never fully paid, and Mohan Lakhamraju later bought back the Indian business, Great Learning Education Services.
mygreatlearning.com.status: Active. Acquired by BYJU'S in 2021; the founders later regained control, with the India unit bought back by co-founder Mohan Lakhamraju

myntra.com.name: Myntra
myntra.com.description: Myntra was set up in 2007 by three IIT Kanpur graduates, Mukesh Bansal, Ashutosh Lawania and Vineet Saxena, and was bought by Flipkart in 2014. It later acquired the fashion site Jabong. Its M-Now service delivers fashion and beauty orders in 30 to 60 minutes in about 10 cities. Myntra reported revenue of ₹6,043 crore for FY25 and has been profitable since FY24. Sharon Pais took charge of the business in April 2026, reporting to Flipkart Group chief executive Kalyan Krishnamurthy.

n26.com.name: N26
n26.com.description: N26 started in Berlin in 2013 and in 2016 became the first digital bank to receive a full German banking licence, so deposits fall under the German deposit protection scheme. It operates in 24 markets and had 5.6 million revenue-relevant customers in 2025. That year revenue passed €500 million, deposits exceeded €10.5 billion and the bank recorded its first full year of net profit. Mike Dargan became chief executive after co-founder Valentin Stalf moved to the supervisory board, and the team numbers about 1,600.

namshi.com.name: Namshi
namshi.com.markets: UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman
namshi.com.description: Namshi has sold fashion online in the Gulf since 2011 and was co-founded by Hisham Zarka and Hosam Arab. Emaar Malls owned it for several years before noon, the e-commerce group backed by Mohamed Alabbar, completed its purchase in February 2023 for Dh1.23 billion. It runs as a separate business within noon and ships to the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman. The site lists more than 2,000 brands across clothing, shoes, beauty and accessories.

netlify.com.name: Netlify
netlify.com.description: Netlify was founded in 2014 by Mathias Biilmann, its chief executive, and Christian Bach, and is based in San Francisco. Developers connect a code repository and Netlify builds and deploys each change, with preview links, serverless functions and a global edge network. In March 2026 it said more than 10 million developers and teams use the platform, and it added Agent Runners, which let users start a web project from a prompt using coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI. It has raised $212 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins.

ninjavan.co.name: Ninja Van
ninjavan.co.markets: Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand
ninjavan.co.description: Ninja Van was started in Singapore in 2014 by Lai Chang Wen, its chief executive, with Shaun Chong and Tan Boxian. It delivers parcels for online sellers and businesses in six markets: Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand. The company says its fleet has grown from one van to more than 5,000 vehicles. Besides last-mile delivery it runs cold chain, B2B restock, freight forwarding and warehousing services, and in Malaysia it launched Ninja Cold for chilled and frozen goods in 2025.

nobroker.in.name: NoBroker
products: Packers and movers, interiors and repairs
nobroker.in.description: NoBroker was founded in Bengaluru in 2013 by Amit Kumar Agarwal, Akhil Gupta and Saurabh Garg. Owners list homes for rent or sale and deal with tenants and buyers without a broker, while paid plans and add-on services such as rental agreements, home loans, moving, interiors, repairs and cleaning bring in revenue. It also runs NoBrokerHood, an app that housing societies use for visitor management and accounts. The company reported revenue of ₹803 crore for FY24 and has raised about $368 million from investors including General Atlantic, Tiger Global and Google.

noom.com.name: Noom
noom.com.description: Noom was founded in New York in 2008 by Saeju Jeong and Artem Petakov. Geoff Cook has been chief executive since 2023, with Jeong as executive chairman. Noom Weight is a psychology-based programme without medication, while Noom Med pairs coaching with prescribed GLP-1 drugs, and a separate Noom for Work offer sells the programmes to employers and health plans. In April 2026 Noom bought Tailor Made Compounding, a licensed 503A pharmacy, and it has since launched a free version of its GLP-1 Companion for patients and providers.

nothing.tech.name: Nothing
products: CMF budget phones, watches and earbuds
nothing.tech.description: Nothing was set up in London in October 2020 by Carl Pei, a co-founder of OnePlus, who remains chief executive. It makes Android phones, earbuds and headphones with see-through casings, and sells cheaper phones, watches and audio under its CMF brand. The company says it has shipped more than five million devices. In September 2025 it raised $200 million in a Series C round led by Tiger Global at a $1.3 billion valuation, with Qualcomm Ventures among the new backers, to fund AI-focused devices planned for 2026.

notion.com.name: Notion
notion.com.description: Notion Labs is based in San Francisco and is led by founder and chief executive Ivan Zhao, with further offices in New York, Dublin, Seoul, Hyderabad, Tokyo and Sydney. Its pages and databases are built from blocks, so the same tool can hold meeting notes, a team wiki or a project tracker. The company says it has 100 million users in more than 50 countries, and recent work has focused on Notion AI and custom agents that automate tasks inside a workspace. In June 2026 it named its first board, made up of independent members, and said it has been profitable from early in its history.

nuvei.com.name: Nuvei
nuvei.com.description: Nuvei processes payments for merchants and platforms, connecting them to more than 200 markets with local acquiring in 53, over 720 alternative payment methods and 150 currencies. Philip Fayer is chair and chief executive. The company listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange in 2020 and on Nasdaq in 2021, then completed a going-private transaction in 2024. It has grown partly by acquisition, buying SafeCharge, Paya and Till Payments among others, and in 2026 it agreed to acquire Payoneer. Nuvei has more than 2,500 staff in over 20 offices.

odoo.com.name: Odoo
odoo.com.description: Odoo was founded in Belgium in 2004 by Fabien Pinckaers, who is still chief executive. Its software comes as a free open source Community edition and a paid Enterprise edition, both built on PostgreSQL with the source code available. Businesses pick from a set of connected apps covering accounting, CRM, inventory, manufacturing, websites and more, and pay per user for the Enterprise version. The company says 12 million people use Odoo, backed by more than 100,000 developers and tens of thousands of community apps, and it has offices in Europe, the Americas, Asia and Australia.

olacabs.com.name: Ola
olacabs.com.description: Ola was started in Bengaluru in December 2010 by Bhavish Aggarwal and Ankit Bhati and is run by ANI Technologies, which renamed the business Ola Consumer in 2024. Its app books bike taxis, auto-rickshaws and cabs for city trips, along with outstation journeys, hourly rentals and Ola for Business corporate travel. The company closed its operations in the UK, Australia and New Zealand in 2024 to concentrate on India, and later wound down its ONDC food and commerce services. Drivers now pay a fixed daily or monthly subscription instead of a commission on each ride.
olacabs.com.status: Active (Ola Cabs renamed Ola Consumer in 2024; international operations closed in 2024)

omio.com.name: Omio
omio.com.markets: Europe, the United States and Canada
omio.com.description: Omio went live in 2013 under the name GoEuro and was founded by Naren Shaam. From one search, travellers compare and book trains, buses, flights and ferries, and the site also handles car hire, airport transfers and rail passes such as the Japan Rail Pass. It works with more than 3,000 transport providers, mainly across Europe, the United States and Canada. Omio has about 300 employees from more than 50 countries, with offices in Berlin, Prague, London, New York and Beijing.

ouraring.com.name: Oura
ouraring.com.description: Oura designs the Oura Ring, a wearable that uses optical heart-rate sensors to measure sleep, activity, stress, heart health and women's health signals, with the results shown in a paid membership app. The company was started in Oulu, Finland, in 2013 and is now headquartered in San Francisco, keeping its EU headquarters in Oulu. It reported 5.7 million paid members in September 2026, after raising $900 million at an $11 billion valuation in 2025. Oura filed to list on Nasdaq in 2026 but postponed the offering that September, citing conditions in the IPO market.
ouraring.com.status: Active (Nasdaq IPO filed and postponed in September 2026)

outschool.com.name: Outschool
outschool.com.description: Outschool runs a marketplace where independent, credentialed teachers offer live online classes and tutoring to children, with classes averaging about four learners per teacher. It was founded in 2015 by Amir Nathoo, Nick Grandy and Mikhail Seregine and says it has served more than 1.5 million school-age children, with over 140,000 classes listed. Nathoo stepped back from running the company in February 2026, and Brian Co, previously a product executive at PowerSchool, was named chief executive in September 2026.

oyorooms.com.name: OYO
oyorooms.com.description: OYO runs a booking app and website for budget and mid-range hotels and vacation homes, and supplies software that partner properties use to manage bookings and prices. Ritesh Agarwal opened the first OYO in Gurugram in 2013, and the business now sits under PRISM, the name its parent Oravel Stays took in 2025. The group's brands include Townhouse, Sunday, Palette, Belvilla, DanCenter and the US chains Motel 6 and Studio 6, with 293,554 storefronts in more than 35 countries at the end of 2025. PRISM filed updated papers with SEBI in 2026 for a planned share listing in India.
oyorooms.com.status: Active (parent PRISM has filed for an IPO in India)

patreon.com.name: Patreon
patreon.com.description: Patreon was started in 2013 by musician Jack Conte and Sam Yam and is based in San Francisco. Artists, podcasters, video makers and writers use it to charge fans a monthly fee for access to their work, and can also offer free memberships. The company says more than 300,000 creators use the platform and that creators have earned over $10 billion through it since launch. More than 10 million fans pay for memberships each month.

paystack.com.name: Paystack
paystack.com.markets: Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa and Côte d'Ivoire
paystack.com.description: Paystack launched in Nigeria in 2016 and was the first Nigerian startup accepted into Y Combinator. Stripe bought the Lagos company in 2020 in a deal reported at over $200 million. It now serves around 300,000 merchants across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa and Côte d'Ivoire. In 2026 it announced The Stack Group, a holding company for Paystack, the Zap consumer transfer app and Paystack Microfinance Bank, subject to regulatory approval.

pedidosya.com.name: PedidosYa
pedidosya.com.description: PedidosYa was founded in Montevideo in 2009 by Ariel Burschtin, Álvaro García and Ruben Sosenke, and Delivery Hero bought it in 2014. Its app takes orders for restaurant meals, groceries and other goods and delivers them through its rider network. It runs in Uruguay, Argentina, Peru, Paraguay, Bolivia and several Central American and Caribbean countries. In 2026 Uber launched a takeover offer for Delivery Hero, with settlement expected in the second half of 2027.

peopleperhour.com.name: PeoplePerHour
peopleperhour.com.description: PeoplePerHour went live in September 2007, set up by engineers Xenios Thrasyvoulou and Simos Kitiris with a focus on UK small businesses. Clients can post a project and receive proposals, or buy fixed-price service offers listed by freelancers, and pay by the hour or by the job. The company describes itself as founder owned and led. It says it has connected more than a million clients and freelancers and paid out over £100 million to freelancers.

pepperfry.com.name: Pepperfry
pepperfry.com.description: Pepperfry was set up in Mumbai in 2011 by former eBay executives Ambareesh Murty and Ashish Shah, and its website went live in January 2012. It sells furniture and home goods online and through a network of more than 100 offline studios. BSE-listed TCC Concept Limited completed its acquisition of a majority stake in December 2025. Pepperfry reported its first profitable quarter in the fourth quarter of FY26.
pepperfry.com.status: Active; acquired by TCC Concept Limited in December 2025

personio.com.name: Personio
personio.com.description: Personio was founded in Munich in 2015 by Hanno Renner, Roman Schumacher, Arseniy Vershinin and Ignaz Forstmeier, and Renner is chief executive. It sells HR and payroll software aimed at organisations with roughly 25 to 5,000 staff. More than 16,000 companies and 1.6 million people use it, and it employs over 1,500 people across six European offices. In 2026 it bought the recruiting AI startup Aurio and the Berlin spend management company Circula, and became a certified B Corp.

pharmeasy.in.name: PharmEasy
pharmeasy.in.description: PharmEasy started in Mumbai in 2015 and is run by API Holdings, the group that also holds a controlling stake in the listed diagnostics firm Thyrocare. Customers use its app and website to order prescription medicines, over-the-counter and wellness products for home delivery, and to book lab tests. Rahul Guha became chief executive in August 2025, when co-founder Siddharth Shah moved to vice-chairman of API Holdings. The group has said an IPO or a merger with Thyrocare remain options once it reaches its profitability target.

plaid.com.name: Plaid
plaid.com.markets: United States, United Kingdom and EU
plaid.com.description: Plaid was founded in 2013 by Zach Perret and William Hockey, and Perret is chief executive. It runs the connections that let finance apps link to a person's bank account to verify it, move money or read balances and transactions with permission. The company says more than 9,000 fintechs build on Plaid and that it supports over 12,000 financial institutions. A share sale in February 2026 was reported to value it at about $8 billion.

pluralsight.com.name: Pluralsight
pluralsight.com.description: Pluralsight was founded in Utah in 2004 by Aaron Skonnard, Fritz Onion, Keith Brown and Bill Williams, and grew for about nine years without outside funding. It sells technology training to individuals and businesses, with more than 6,500 courses, skill assessments and hands-on labs covering software, cloud, AI and security. The company says over 23,000 organisations use it. Vista Equity Partners bought it in 2021, a lender group led by Blue Owl took control in 2024, and it set up a new headquarters in Westlake, Texas in 2025.
pluralsight.com.status: Active; owned by a lender group led by Blue Owl Capital since 2024

poshmark.com.name: Poshmark
poshmark.com.description: Poshmark was founded in 2011 by Manish Chandra, Chetan Pungaliya, Gautam Golwala and Tracy Sun and is based in Redwood City, California. Sellers list clothing, shoes, accessories and home items from a phone, and buyers can also shop through live selling shows. The company says it has over 130 million members in the US and Canada and that more than 350 million items have sold. South Korea's Naver bought it for $1.2 billion in January 2023, and Naver executive Namsun Kim became chief executive in October 2025.
poshmark.com.status: Active; acquired by Naver in January 2023

practo.com.name: Practo
practo.com.markets: India, the US and the UAE
practo.com.description: Practo was founded in 2008 by Shashank ND and Abhinav Lal and is based in Bengaluru. Patients use its app to find doctors, book clinic visits, consult online and order lab tests and medicines, while clinics and hospitals use its Ray and Insta software to run their practices. It has expanded from India into the US and the UAE. Jagnoor Singh is chief executive and Shashank ND is executive chairman, and a public listing has been reported as planned for 2027.

prodigygame.com.name: Prodigy Education
prodigygame.com.description: Prodigy Education began in 2011 as an undergraduate project by Alex Peters and Rohan Mahimker, who still lead the company as co-chief executives. Its games put elementary school pupils on quests in a fantasy world where progress depends on answering curriculum-aligned questions. Teachers can use Prodigy Math free of charge, and the company earns money from optional paid memberships for families. It has raised funding from TPG Growth and the Canadian Business Growth Fund.

propertyfinder.ae.name: Property Finder
products: Property listings for sale and rent
propertyfinder.ae.description: Property Finder was founded in Dubai in 2007 by Michael Lahyani, who remains chief executive. Its website and app list homes and commercial property for sale and rent from agents and developers in the UAE and other Middle East and North Africa markets. It also offers a home valuation tool and a credit score service for buyers. In January 2026 it raised $170 million in a round led by Mubadala, after a $525 million investment led by Permira in 2025.

propertyguru.com.sg.name: PropertyGuru
propertyguru.com.sg.ownership: Subsidiary of EQT Private Capital Asia
propertyguru.com.sg.description: PropertyGuru started in Singapore in 2007 and now runs property listing sites across four Southeast Asian countries. Its brands include PropertyGuru in Singapore and Malaysia, iProperty in Malaysia, DDproperty in Thailand and Batdongsan in Vietnam, alongside tools for agents and the Asia Property Awards. EQT Private Capital Asia bought the group for about $1.1 billion in December 2024 and took it off the New York Stock Exchange. Lewis Ng has been chief executive since March 2025, and the group had more than 1,200 staff at the end of 2025.
propertyguru.com.sg.status: Active; taken private by EQT in December 2024

proton.me.name: Proton
proton.me.description: Proton was started in Geneva in 2014 by scientists who met at CERN, and co-founder Andy Yen is chief executive. It began with the encrypted email service Proton Mail and has added a VPN, cloud storage, a password manager, calendar, documents and an AI assistant called Lumo. The company passed 100 million registered users in early 2026. Since 2024 its main shareholder has been the non-profit Proton Foundation, and it has no venture capital investors.

public.com.name: Public
public.com.description: Public is a New York brokerage run by co-founders and co-chief executives Leif Abraham and Jannick Malling. Its app and website let US customers trade stocks, ETFs, options and crypto, buy corporate bonds and Treasuries, and hold cash and retirement accounts. The broker-dealer, Open to the Public Investing, is a FINRA member, and Public Advisors is an SEC-registered investment adviser. It promotes AI tools that summarise earnings calls and can act on a customer's instructions.

purplle.com.name: Purplle
purplle.com.description: Purplle was founded in Mumbai in 2012 by Manish Taneja, Rahul Dash and Suyash Katyayani, and the business is run by Manash Lifestyle Private Limited. It sells makeup, skincare, haircare and body care from Indian and international brands through its app and website, alongside beauty brands it owns. The company has raised about $480 million across several funding rounds, most recently in October 2024.

qonto.com.name: Qonto
qonto.com.markets: France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Austria, Belgium, Portugal and the Netherlands
qonto.com.description: Qonto was founded in Paris in 2017 by Alexandre Prot and Steve Anavi. It provides online business accounts, payment cards, invoicing and bookkeeping tools to small companies and freelancers in eight European countries. Qonto SA holds a payment institution licence from the French regulator ACPR, granted in 2018. The company says it has more than 750,000 customers and about 1,700 employees.

quintoandar.com.br.name: QuintoAndar
quintoandar.com.br.markets: Brazil, plus Argentina, Mexico, Peru, Ecuador and Panama through its portals
quintoandar.com.br.description: QuintoAndar runs a property platform in Brazil that handles home rentals end to end, from listings and visits to digital contracts, and pays landlords a guaranteed monthly rent. Gabriel Braga and André Penha founded it in Campinas in December 2012, and it added home buying and selling in 2020. In 2021 it bought the property portals of Argentina's Navent, including Imovelweb, Inmuebles24 and Zonaprop, which took it into five more Latin American countries. In 2026 it announced R$2 billion of technology spending over two years, mostly on artificial intelligence, and a move to a new São Paulo headquarters in Vila Leopoldina.

quizlet.com.name: Quizlet
quizlet.com.description: Quizlet offers study tools built around flashcard sets, practice tests and classroom games, with free and paid subscriptions for students and teachers. Andrew Sutherland started it in 2005 to prepare for a high school French vocabulary quiz, and the company is based in San Francisco under chief executive Kurt Beidler. It says more than 60 million students, teachers and other learners use the platform. In February 2026 it bought Coconote, an app that turns lecture recordings into notes, quizzes and flashcards, and launched new AI study features at the same time.

quora.com.name: Quora
quora.com.description: Quora runs a question-and-answer website and mobile apps, and since 2023 has also operated Poe, a separate service where people chat with AI models from several developers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Mistral. Adam D'Angelo, formerly Facebook's chief technology officer, started Quora with Charlie Cheever in 2009 and remains its chief executive. Poe uses a freemium model with a paid subscription, and developers who build bots on it can earn money per query. Quora raised $75 million from Andreessen Horowitz in 2024 to expand Poe.

ramp.com.name: Ramp
ramp.com.description: Ramp sells corporate cards together with software for expenses, bill payments, procurement, accounts receivable and automated bookkeeping, used mainly by US businesses. Eric Glyman, Karim Atiyeh and Gene Lee founded the company in 2019, and it is based in New York with Glyman as chief executive. By October 2026 it reported more than 85,000 business customers, annualised revenue above $2 billion and about 1,900 staff. That month it raised money at a $60 billion valuation in a round led by Dragoneer, and it has added tools that track what companies spend on AI services.

rapido.bike.name: Rapido
rapido.bike.description: Rapido runs a ride-hailing app in India that books bike taxis, auto rickshaws and cabs, serving smaller cities as well as the metros. Aravind Sanka, Pavan Guntupalli and Rishikesh SR founded it in 2015, and it is based in Bengaluru, trading through Roppen Transportation Services Private Limited. It also runs Ownly, a food delivery app piloted in Bengaluru that charges restaurants no commission and bills customers a delivery fee instead. In May 2026 Rapido raised $240 million in a round led by Prosus at a $3 billion valuation.

rappi.com.name: Rappi
rappi.com.description: Rappi runs a delivery app in nine Latin American countries, including Mexico, Colombia, Brazil, Argentina and Chile, taking orders from more than 125,000 partner restaurants as well as grocery and pharmacy stores. Its Turbo service aims to deliver in under ten minutes from more than 235 Turbo stores in the region. Simón Borrero, Sebastián Mejía and Felipe Villamarín started the company in Bogotá in 2015, and Borrero is chief executive. Rappi says it has more than 35 million active users, 350,000 active couriers and 5,200 direct employees, and it has raised over US$2.2 billion from investors including SoftBank and Sequoia Capital.

razorpay.com.name: Razorpay
razorpay.com.markets: India, Malaysia, Singapore and the US
razorpay.com.description: Razorpay sells payment and banking software to Indian businesses, covering its payment gateway, payment links, subscriptions, point-of-sale devices and Magic Checkout, plus current accounts, payouts and corporate cards through RazorpayX. Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar, both IIT Roorkee graduates, founded it in 2014, and it is based in Bengaluru. It also offers business lending through Razorpay Capital and payroll software, and operates in Malaysia under the Curlec brand. In November 2026 it received a final licence from IFSCA to handle cross-border money movement from GIFT City.

redbus.in.name: redBus
redbus.in.markets: India, Southeast Asia (Indonesia, Singapore, Malaysia, Cambodia, Vietnam), Colombia and Peru
redbus.in.description: redBus sells intercity bus tickets on its website and app, listing seats from thousands of bus operators, and also books train tickets through its redRail app. It began in 2006 and is now one of the brands of MakeMyTrip, the Nasdaq-listed travel group that also runs MakeMyTrip and Goibibo. Outside India it runs local sites in Indonesia, Singapore, Malaysia, Cambodia, Vietnam, Colombia and Peru. The company says it has served more than 56 million customers and works with over 5,200 bus operators across more than 730,000 routes.

ridedott.com.name: Dott
ridedott.com.markets: 20 countries in Europe and the Middle East
ridedott.com.description: Dott rents shared electric scooters and e-bikes by the minute through its app in cities across Europe and the Middle East. Henri Moissinac and Maxim Romain founded it in Amsterdam in 2018, and in 2024 it merged with Berlin-based TIER Mobility, after which TIER riders and vehicles moved over to the Dott app and brand. The combined company reported about 200,000 vehicles in 400 cities and 20 countries, with 76.9 million rides and €173.3 million in net revenue in 2025. Maxim Romain is chief executive and Henri Moissinac is executive chairman.

rippling.com.name: Rippling
products: Global payroll and employer of record
rippling.com.description: Rippling sells one platform for the people and back-office side of a business, covering HR records, payroll, benefits, recruiting, device and identity management, corporate cards, bill pay and travel. Co-founder Parker Conrad is chief executive, and the company is based in San Francisco with offices in the US, UK, Ireland, India, Australia, Canada and Singapore. Its global payroll and employer-of-record services let customers hire and pay staff and contractors in other countries. Rippling has raised $1.8 billion from investors including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund and Sequoia, and opened an AI lab in Bengaluru in September 2026.

satispay.com.name: Satispay
products: Investing in funds, stocks and ETFs
satispay.com.markets: Italy, with operations in Luxembourg and Spain
satispay.com.description: Satispay runs a mobile payment network in Italy that people use to pay in shops and online, send money to contacts and pay public bills through the PagoPA system. Beyond payments, its app offers investment funds, stocks and ETFs, an interest-paying money box, instalment payments and a card, while its SatisWelfare unit supplies meal and shopping vouchers to employers. The company is run from Milan, and its payment licence is held by Satispay Europe S.A., an e-money institution registered with Luxembourg's CSSF. It says it has 6.5 million users and more than 750 staff, with offices in Milan, Luxembourg, Barcelona and Naples.

scalable.capital.name: Scalable Capital
scalable.capital.description: Scalable Capital runs an investing app and website from Germany, combining Scalable Broker, for trading stocks, ETFs, funds, crypto and derivatives, with Scalable Wealth, a digital asset management service. It was founded in 2014 by Erik Podzuweit, Florian Prucker, Adam French and Stefan Mittnik, and its team works from Munich, Berlin and London. The business now operates as Scalable Capital Bank GmbH, based in Munich, and also offers overnight and fixed-term savings, credit and retirement products. It has raised €470 million in equity from investors including BlackRock, Tencent, Balderton and HV Capital.

sharechat.com.name: ShareChat
sharechat.com.description: ShareChat is built by Mohalla Tech, a Bengaluru company that launched the app in October 2015 for people who prefer to post and browse in Indian languages rather than English. The app works in 14 languages, including Hindi, Tamil, Bhojpuri and Haryanvi. Mohalla Tech also runs the Moj short-video app and QuickTV, a subscription service for short serial dramas. Revenue for the 2025-26 financial year rose about 40% to roughly Rs 1,016 crore, and the company has said it is preparing for a stock market listing.

shiprocket.in.name: Shiprocket
shiprocket.in.markets: India, with international shipping to 220+ countries and territories
shiprocket.in.description: Shiprocket started in 2017 as a shipping tool for small online sellers and now runs a wider set of services from its Gurugram corporate office, including warehousing and fulfilment, cross-border shipping, a one-click checkout called Fastrr and working-capital lending. It says it serves more than 2.5 lakh online retailers and reaches over 19,000 Indian pin codes through 17-plus courier partners. The company listed its shares on the NSE and BSE on 19 August 2026, debuting at about 35% above its Rs 97 issue price.
shiprocket.in.status: Active. Listed on NSE and BSE in August 2026

simplilearn.com.name: Simplilearn
simplilearn.com.description: Simplilearn sells online courses and longer programmes in areas such as data science, AI, cloud computing, cybersecurity, project management and digital marketing, many of them run with universities including Purdue, Caltech CTME and UMass Amherst, and with Indian institutes such as IIT Roorkee and IIM Indore. Courses mix recorded material with live online classes. Founded in Bengaluru in 2010, it also has offices in Plano, Texas and Singapore. Blackstone bought a controlling stake in 2021 for $250 million, and the company now describes itself as a Blackstone company.

siteground.com.name: SiteGround
siteground.com.description: SiteGround was started in 2004 by a group of university friends in Sofia and has stayed privately owned, with no outside shareholders. It runs its service from data centres in the United States, Europe, Singapore and Australia, and says it manages more than three million domains. Alongside hosting it has built its own tools, including a site builder, an AI website and web app builder called Coderick AI, and a standalone email marketing service. The group has companies registered in the USA, UK, Spain, Cyprus and Bulgaria and more than 500 staff.

skillshare.com.name: Skillshare
skillshare.com.description: Skillshare runs a subscription library of short video classes taught by working creatives, covering subjects such as illustration, graphic design, photography, video, writing and freelancing. Most classes end with a hands-on project that students post for others to see. Anyone can apply to teach, and teachers are paid from the subscription revenue. The company was founded in New York in November 2010 and first ran in-person local classes before moving fully to online video.

skyscanner.net.name: Skyscanner
skyscanner.net.description: Skyscanner grew out of a spreadsheet of flight prices that three friends built in Edinburgh, and the company was formed in 2003. It does not sell tickets itself. Searches return fares and rates from more than 1,200 airlines, travel agents, hotel sites and rental firms, and the user books with the chosen provider. The company says more than 100 million people use its website and app each month. China's Ctrip, now Trip.com Group, bought Skyscanner in 2016 for about $1.75 billion, and it keeps offices in Edinburgh, Barcelona, Miami and Singapore.

snapdeal.com.name: Snapdeal
snapdeal.com.description: Snapdeal was founded in 2010 by Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal and now concentrates on lower-priced fashion, home and lifestyle goods for shoppers in smaller towns and cities. In the 2025-26 financial year it delivered to 18,972 pin codes. The marketplace belongs to AceVector, the renamed group company that also owns the Unicommerce e-commerce software business and Stellaro Brands, a consumer brands unit. AceVector listed on the NSE and BSE in October 2026.
snapdeal.com.status: Active. Parent AceVector listed on NSE and BSE in October 2026

soundcloud.com.name: SoundCloud
products: SoundCloud Go and Go+ listener plans
soundcloud.com.description: SoundCloud was founded in Berlin in 2007 by Swedish sound designer Alexander Ljung and musician Eric Wahlforss as a place for musicians to share recordings. Anyone can upload, and the company says more than 40 million creators use it, which gives it a large catalogue of remixes, DJ sets and early releases. Listeners can stream free with ads or pay for Go or Go+, while artists can buy a subscription that bundles distribution to other services. Eliah Seton has been chief executive since 2023, and in July 2026 the company bought the independent music platform Nina Protocol.

squarespace.com.name: Squarespace
squarespace.com.description: Squarespace sells subscription software for building and running websites, with design templates, an AI site builder, domain registration, online stores, invoicing and email marketing in one account. It also owns Acuity Scheduling, an appointment booking tool. Anthony Casalena started the company in his university dorm room at the University of Maryland in 2003 and still runs it. Investment firm Permira took Squarespace private in October 2024 in a deal worth about $7.2 billion, ending its listing on the New York Stock Exchange. It has offices in New York, Dublin and Aveiro in Portugal.
squarespace.com.status: Active. Taken private by Permira in October 2024

squareyards.com.name: Square Yards
squareyards.com.description: Square Yards was set up in Gurugram in 2014 by Tanuj Shori and Kanika Gupta Shori and earns most of its money from brokering new and resale homes. Over time it has added Urban Money for mortgages, Azuro for rentals and property management, Interior Company for home interiors, and PropVR for 3D and virtual reality tours. India produced 88% of revenue in the 2025-26 financial year, with the rest from the UAE, Australia and Canada. Group revenue that year was about Rs 2,086 crore, and the company has hired banks for a planned stock market listing.

starlingbank.com.name: Starling Bank
products: Marketplace for insurance, pensions and accounting tools
starlingbank.com.description: Starling Bank is a UK bank with no branches, offering personal, joint, business, multi-currency and children's accounts through its app, and it is authorised by the PRA and regulated by the FCA and PRA. It was established in June 2014 and is based in London, with further offices in Cardiff, Southampton and Manchester, and Raman Bhatia is group chief executive. Through Engine by Starling it licenses its banking software to other companies that want to build their own banking products. Starling says it holds more than four million accounts, and in 2026 it added a student account, expense cards for small businesses and plans for a business credit card.

stockx.com.name: StockX
stockx.com.description: StockX runs an online marketplace where people buy and sell sneakers, streetwear, trading cards, collectibles, handbags, watches and consumer electronics at prices set by live bids and asks, much like a stock exchange. It publishes real-time price data for each item, and its listings cover hundreds of brands, including Jordan Brand, Nike, adidas and Supreme. Goods pass through StockX's own offices and authentication centres on the way from seller to buyer. The company was founded in Detroit in 2016, is still headquartered there and handles sales to buyers around the world.

substack.com.name: Substack
substack.com.description: Substack runs a publishing platform and app where writers, podcasters and video creators send their work to subscribers by email and in the app, and can charge readers for paid subscriptions. Chris Best, Hamish McKenzie and Jairaj Sethi founded it in 2017, and it is based in San Francisco. Its tools include Notes, live video, a recording studio and the Substack Reader, and it offers legal help to writers through Substack Defender. Publications on the platform include The Bulwark, Lenny's Newsletter and Silver Bulletin, and the company says paid subscriptions across Substack have passed five million.

sumup.com.name: SumUp
sumup.com.description: SumUp was launched in August 2012 and is based in London, where its UK business trades as SumUp Payments Limited, an electronic money institution authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority. Alongside card readers and its point-of-sale system, it offers business accounts, personal accounts with cashback, loyalty tools and a developer platform for payment integrations. The company says it serves more than 4 million businesses with a team of about 3,000 people working from 26 offices. Canada became its 38th market.

supercell.com.name: Supercell
supercell.com.description: Supercell Oy was founded in Helsinki in 2010 and keeps its head office in the city's Jätkäsaari district, with further studios and offices in London, Shanghai, Seoul and San Francisco. Its free-to-play catalogue also includes Boom Beach, Squad Busters and mo.co. Tencent became the majority owner in 2016, when it bought SoftBank's controlling stake in an $8.6 billion deal. For 2025 the company reported revenue of €2.65 billion on its non-deferred measure and a headcount of 890 after almost 300 hires.

takealot.com.name: Takealot
takealot.com.description: Takealot.com began trading online in 2011 and is run from Cape Town, with distribution centres in Cape Town and Johannesburg. It is the main business of the Naspers-owned Takealot Group, which also runs the Mr D food delivery service and a fulfilment arm for marketplace sellers. The group sold its Superbalist fashion site to a private equity consortium in September 2024. Shoppers can join TakealotMore, a paid subscription programme, and in the six months to September 2025 Takealot.com revenue grew 32% to R6.7 billion.

tamara.co.name: Tamara
tamara.co.description: Tamara was started in Riyadh in late 2020 by Abdulmajeed Alsukhan, Turki Bin Zarah and Abdulmohsen Albabtain. Saudi Arabia is its home market, and it also serves shoppers in the UAE and Kuwait through online checkouts and a card that works at physical shops. In December 2023 a $340 million Series C round made it the first Saudi fintech valued above $1 billion. By September 2025 it reported more than 20 million customers and 87,000 merchants, when it secured an asset-backed facility of up to $2.4 billion from Goldman Sachs, Citi and Apollo funds.

telegram.org.name: Telegram
telegram.org.description: Telegram launched on iOS in August 2013 and on Android later that year. Pavel Durov funds the service and his brother Nikolai leads the technology, with the development team now based in Dubai after earlier moves through Berlin, London and Singapore. The app says it has more than 1 billion active users. Groups can hold up to 200,000 members and channels have no subscriber limit. Its income comes from sponsored messages in large public channels, added in 2021, and the Telegram Premium subscription, added in 2022.

toptal.com.name: Toptal
toptal.com.description: Toptal was started in November 2010 by Taso Du Val and Breanden Beneschott, who built its first matching tools in a Princeton dorm room, and it was registered as Toptal LLC that year. The company has never had a head office and works fully remotely, with its talent network spread over more than 140 countries. Beyond software engineering it places specialists in AI and data science, product management, marketing and sales. It also runs HireGlobal for international payroll and compliance, and Graphite and NSI for finance and creative work.

toss.im.name: Toss
toss.im.description: Toss is run by Viva Republica, a Seoul company founded in 2013 by Lee Seung-gun, a former dentist who is still its chief executive. The app began with simple money transfers and now links to group businesses that include the internet-only Toss Bank, the brokerage Toss Securities, Toss Payments and Toss Insurance. It passed 30 million users in 2025, the same year it launched in Australia. The company has said it is preparing a United States stock market listing.

traderepublic.com.name: Trade Republic
traderepublic.com.description: Trade Republic has been building its business in Berlin since 2015 and opened its investing app to the public in 2019. It holds a full banking licence granted by the European Central Bank in 2023 and is supervised by BaFin and the Bundesbank. Customers can invest from €1, earn interest on uninvested cash and use a card that pays 1% back into their investments. In December 2025 it reported more than 10 million customers and about €150 billion in assets, when a €1.2 billion secondary share sale valued it at €12.5 billion.

trading212.com.name: Trading 212
trading212.com.description: Trading 212 has been operating since 2004 and runs its UK business as Trading 212 UK Ltd, which is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority. Sister companies in Cyprus, Bulgaria, Germany and Australia hold licences from CySEC, the Bulgarian Financial Supervision Commission, BaFin and ASIC. Its staff work from offices that include London, Sofia, Plovdiv, Limassol, Berlin, Dublin and Sydney. Group accounts for 2025 showed revenue up 70% to £345.8 million and an average of 722 employees, and a UK pension product was added in May 2026.

traveloka.com.name: Traveloka
traveloka.com.markets: Southeast Asia, Australia, Japan and South Korea
traveloka.com.description: Traveloka was set up in Jakarta in 2012 by Ferry Unardi, Derianto Kusuma and a school friend, Albert, with seed money from East Ventures. It runs local operations in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, Australia, Japan and South Korea, and lists hotels and activities in more than 100 countries. Its app sells over 20 types of product, from flights and Whoosh high-speed rail tickets to cruises, eSIMs and travel insurance. The company says the app has been downloaded more than 140 million times.

trezor.io.name: Trezor
trezor.io.description: Trezor was started in Prague in 2013 by Marek Palatinus and Pavol Rusnák, who also co-founded its parent group SatoshiLabs. The first device, the Trezor Model One, went on sale in 2014, and the range has since grown through the Model T and the Safe 3, Safe 5 and Safe 7. Owners manage their coins with the Trezor Suite app for desktop and mobile, and the company also sells Keep Metal, a steel plate for storing a recovery phrase. The company says its team has more than 110 people.

trustly.com.name: Trustly
trustly.com.description: Trustly was founded in Stockholm in 2008 and lets people pay online straight from their bank account. Trustly Group AB is a payment institution supervised by Sweden's Finansinspektionen, and the group also holds FCA authorisations in the UK and owns SlimPay in France. Nordic Capital has been its main shareholder since 2018, alongside Alfvén & Didrikson and BlackRock Private Equity Partners. The company employs about 900 people across offices that include London, Barcelona, Malta, Ottawa and San Carlos in California, and says it works with more than 9,000 merchants.

turo.com.name: Turo
products: Protection plans for hosts and guests
turo.com.markets: US, Canada, UK, France and Australia
turo.com.description: Turo has run its car sharing marketplace since 2010 and lets private owners and small rental businesses list vehicles that guests book through its website and apps. It operates in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France and Australia, with offices in San Francisco, Phoenix, Toronto, London, Paris and Sydney. By September 2024 it reported about 150,000 active hosts, 3.5 million active guests and 350,000 active listings. The company filed to go public in 2022 but withdrew the plan in February 2025 and remains privately held.

udacity.com.name: Udacity
products: Enterprise training via Digital Competency Platform
udacity.com.description: Udacity grew out of a free online version of Stanford's Introduction to Artificial Intelligence course, taught by Sebastian Thrun and Peter Norvig in 2011, and it now operates as part of Accenture. Learners work through projects that are reviewed by a network of more than 700 industry mentors, and the company also sells training programmes to employers and governments. It reports more than 16.9 million registered users in over 240 countries and 205,000 Nanodegree certificates awarded. Degree options now include a Master of Science in AI.

unacademy.com.name: Unacademy
unacademy.com.description: Unacademy started as a YouTube channel in 2010 and became an online learning company in 2015, run by Sorting Hat Technologies from Bengaluru. Its educators teach live and recorded classes for Indian entrance and government exams such as UPSC, JEE, NEET and GATE. upGrad completed its purchase of Unacademy in September 2026 in an all-stock deal valued at just over $200 million. PrepLadder, Graphy and Airlearn continue to run under their own names, and in November 2026 co-founder Gaurav Munjal became executive chairman with Akhilendra Kumar taking over as chief executive.

upbit.com.name: Upbit
upbit.com.description: Upbit is the cryptocurrency exchange run by Dunamu, a Seoul company, and lets customers in South Korea buy and sell digital assets against the Korean won. New tokens often launch on the exchange with won trading pairs, as AZTEC did in February 2026. Dunamu also unveiled GIWA, a layer-2 blockchain, in September 2025. In November 2025 Bloomberg reported that Dunamu would be brought under Naver Financial, the finance arm of the internet group Naver, through a share swap, with a Nasdaq listing of the combined business planned afterwards.

upgrad.com.name: upGrad
upgrad.com.description: upGrad sells online degrees, postgraduate diplomas and certificate courses run with universities in India and abroad, alongside study abroad programmes and corporate training through upGrad Enterprise. It was started in Mumbai in 2015 by Ronnie Screwvala, Mayank Kumar, Phalgun Kompalli and Ravijot Chugh. In FY26 it reported gross revenue of about Rs 2,070 crore and more than 100,000 learners enrolled at any one time. The company has agreed to acquire Internshala and Unacademy, and Screwvala has said it intends to list on the stock market in 2027.

upstox.com.name: Upstox
upstox.com.description: Upstox runs a trading and investing app for Indian retail investors, covering equities, futures and options, commodities, IPOs, mutual funds and fixed deposits. The broking business operates as Upstox Securities Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of RKSV Securities India, and was co-founded by Ravi Kumar, Kavitha Subramanian and Shrini Viswanath. The company says it has more than 2 crore customers. Tiger Global is among its investors, and in August 2026 the company was reported to be in talks with bankers about a public listing.

urbanladder.com.name: Urban Ladder
urbanladder.com.description: Urban Ladder started in Bengaluru in 2012 selling furniture online and later opened its own stores in several Indian cities. Its range covers sofas, beds, dining and study furniture, storage, mattresses and home decor such as lighting, rugs and wall art. Reliance Retail bought a 96 per cent stake in 2020 for about Rs 182 crore, and the website now names Reliance Retail Limited as the operating entity. The company was founded by Ashish Goel and Rajiv Srivatsa.

vedantu.com.name: Vedantu
products: Live online classes for school students
vedantu.com.description: Vedantu was set up in 2014 by Vamsi Krishna, Pulkit Jain and Anand Prakash and is based in Bengaluru. It teaches school students up to Class 12 through live online classes and runs coaching for JEE and NEET, along with crash courses for exams such as CUET and NDA. It also runs offline and hybrid learning centres, and in 2022 it bought the Karnataka coaching chain Deeksha, which now trades as Deeksha Vedantu. The company reported a profitable fourth quarter in FY25 after several years of cost cutting.

vercel.com.name: Vercel
vercel.com.description: Vercel provides a cloud platform where developers deploy websites and web apps, with hosting, a global content delivery network, serverless compute and observability tools built in. Guillermo Rauch founded the company in 2015, and it maintains the open-source Next.js framework, which recorded more than 500 million downloads in the year to September 2025. Newer products include v0, which generates app code from text prompts, and the AI SDK for adding AI features to applications. In September 2025 Vercel raised a $300 million Series F co-led by Accel and GIC at a $9.3 billion valuation.

vinted.com.name: Vinted
vinted.com.description: Vinted runs an online marketplace and app where people sell and buy secondhand clothes, shoes, accessories, children's items and homeware. It was founded in Vilnius in 2008 by Justas Janauskas and Milda Mitkutė and is now available in 26 countries, mostly in Europe, after launching in Latvia, Estonia and Slovenia in 2025. The wider Vinted Group also runs Vinted Go, a parcel delivery network, and Vinted Pay for payments. In 2025 the group reported revenue of €1.1 billion, up 38 per cent, on €10.8 billion of gross merchandise value.

voi.com.name: Voi
voi.com.description: Voi rents shared electric scooters and e-bikes that riders find and unlock through its app. It was founded in Stockholm in 2018 and now runs more than 200,000 vehicles in over 130 towns and cities across 13 countries, with around 1,000 staff. Riders have taken more than 500 million trips on Voi vehicles since launch, and the company counts over 4 million active riders a year. In the third quarter of 2026 it reported net revenue of €88.2 million, up 53 per cent on a year earlier.

vultr.com.name: Vultr
vultr.com.description: Vultr sells cloud infrastructure to developers and businesses, including virtual machines, bare metal servers, cloud GPUs, managed Kubernetes, load balancers and block and object storage. David Aninowsky founded the company in 2014, and it was self-funded for more than a decade before taking outside investment. It runs 32 cloud data centre regions and has customers in 185 countries. In December 2024 it raised equity from LuminArx and AMD Ventures at a $3.5 billion valuation, followed by $329 million in credit financing in June 2025 to expand its AI capacity.

wallapop.com.name: Wallapop
wallapop.com.description: Wallapop runs a marketplace app where individuals buy and sell used goods, either collecting nearby or having items shipped. It was founded in Barcelona in 2013, where it is still based, and expanded into Italy in 2021 and Portugal in 2022. The platform has more than 19 million monthly active users. South Korea's NAVER, which already held 29.5 per cent, agreed in August 2025 to buy the remaining 70.5 per cent for €377 million, and the acquisition completed in January 2026.

wealthsimple.com.name: Wealthsimple
products: Self-directed trading in stocks, ETFs and options
wealthsimple.com.description: Wealthsimple offers Canadians self-directed trading in stocks, ETFs, options and crypto, managed portfolios, registered accounts such as TFSAs and RRSPs, chequing and savings, a credit card, mortgages and tax filing software. It was founded in Toronto in 2014 and is led by co-founder and chief executive Michael Katchen. The company reported C$169.2 billion in assets under administration at the end of September 2026 and more than 4 million clients. In October 2026 it announced a funding round of up to C$425 million led by GIC at a C$13.8 billion valuation.

webflow.com.name: Webflow
webflow.com.description: Webflow makes a browser-based visual tool for designing, building and hosting websites, with a content management system, ecommerce, localisation and SEO features in the same product. Vlad and Sergie Magdalin co-founded it in 2013, and the company is based in San Francisco with staff working in 18 countries. It says more than 300,000 organisations use the platform. Webflow has raised $335 million from investors including Accel and CapitalG, and in March 2026 it acquired Vidoso.ai as it added AI agent tools for marketing teams.

wellfound.com.name: Wellfound
wellfound.com.description: Wellfound runs a hiring marketplace for startups, where companies post jobs free of charge and candidates apply to roles at early-stage and growing technology firms, many of them remote. It began inside AngelList as AngelList Talent and became a separate company, AL Talent, Inc., under the Wellfound name in November 2022, with Amit Matani as chief executive. Paid products include Reach, which sources candidates with AI, and Autopilot, a managed recruiting service. In January 2026 it bought the AI recruiting tool Hirefly, and it says more than 10 million candidates have opted in to the platform.

wework.com.name: WeWork
wework.com.description: WeWork leases flexible workspace, from hot desks and dedicated desks to private offices, full floors and meeting rooms, with memberships such as All Access and On Demand for people who move between sites. Its website lists around 600 locations in more than 100 cities. The company filed for Chapter 11 in November 2023 and emerged in June 2024 as a private company with Yardi Systems as its majority owner. It is led by chief executive John Santora, a former Cushman & Wakefield executive.
wework.com.status: Active (emerged from Chapter 11 in June 2024, now privately owned)

withings.com.name: Withings
products: Smart scales with body composition and ECG
Withings Health Solutions remote patient monitoring
withings.com.description: Withings designs connected health devices for home use, including scales that measure body composition and ECG, hybrid smartwatches, blood pressure monitors and sleep trackers that sync to its app. Eric Carreel co-founded the French company in 2008, sold it to Nokia in 2016 and bought it back in 2018. About two thirds of its 2025 revenue came from FDA-cleared medical devices, and it reports 15 million active users with a team of around 400. Its Withings Health Solutions arm supplies remote patient monitoring to healthcare providers, and the United States is its largest market.

wolt.com.name: Wolt
wolt.com.description: Wolt runs a delivery app for ordering from restaurants, grocery shops and other retailers, and it also operates its own Wolt Market grocery stores, the Wolt+ subscription and Wolt Drive, a delivery service for other businesses. Six co-founders started the company in Helsinki in 2014, and it now works in more than 30 countries and over 1,000 cities. DoorDash completed its acquisition of Wolt in May 2022. The company says it has more than 15,000 employees and over 290,000 courier partners.

wordpress.com.name: WordPress.com
wordpress.com.description: WordPress.com is run by Automattic, a company formed in 2005 that has worked as a fully distributed, remote-first business since the start. The service gives people and businesses a hosted version of the open-source WordPress software, with plans covering blogs, newsletters, online stores, agency hosting and enterprise sites through WordPress VIP. Automattic says its 1,347 staff speak 106 languages, and its other products include WooCommerce, Jetpack, Tumblr, Day One and Pocket Casts. Its mobile app for managing sites is published under the Jetpack name.

workana.com.name: Workana
workana.com.description: Workana runs an online marketplace that connects businesses with remote freelancers, mostly across Spanish and Portuguese speaking Latin America. Clients post projects, compare proposals from registered professionals and pay through the platform. The company was founded in Buenos Aires in 2012 by Tomás O'Farrell, Guillermo Bracciaforte, Fernando Fornales and Mariano Iglesias, and began operating in Brazil in 2013, which later became its largest market. Workana says more than 10 million professionals have registered on the site.

worldremit.com.name: WorldRemit
worldremit.com.description: WorldRemit lets people living abroad send money home through its app and website, with transfers paid into bank accounts and mobile money wallets, collected at cash pickup points or sent as airtime top-up. It was founded in 2010 by Ismail Ahmed, Catherine Wines and Richard Igoe, and its global headquarters are in London. WorldRemit is one of two remittance brands owned by Zepz, alongside Sendwave, and the group reports more than 9 million customers in over 130 countries. Its UK operating company, WorldRemit Ltd, is incorporated in England and Wales.

wpengine.com.name: WP Engine
wpengine.com.description: WP Engine provides managed hosting and developer tools for websites built on WordPress, from small business sites to large ecommerce and media operations. Jason Cohen founded it in Austin, Texas in 2010, and the company reports more than 1.5 million customers in over 150 countries and more than 1,000 staff across the Americas, Europe and Asia Pacific. It has grown through acquisitions including Flywheel, StudioPress, Delicious Brains and NitroPack, and it maintains the Local development app and the Advanced Custom Fields plugin. Private equity firm Silver Lake took a $250 million stake in the business in 2018.

wuzzuf.net.name: WUZZUF
products: Job search apps for iOS and Android
wuzzuf.net.description: WUZZUF is a recruitment site run by Cairo based BasharSoft, which Ameer Sherif co-founded in 2009. Employers use it to post vacancies, search CVs and buy recruitment services, while job seekers build profiles and apply through the website or its iOS and Android apps. The site launched in 2012 and focuses mainly on white-collar roles in Egypt, and it also lists jobs in Saudi Arabia. WUZZUF says it has served more than 55,000 companies in Egypt and that over 1.5 million candidates have been hired through it.

wyzant.com.name: Wyzant
wyzant.com.description: Wyzant runs a tutoring marketplace in the United States where students and parents search tutor profiles and book lessons online or in person. Subjects range from school maths, science and test preparation such as the SAT to languages, music and computing. The company was founded in 2005 by Mike Weishuhn and Andrew Geant and is based in Chicago. IXL Learning acquired it in 2021 and Wyzant now operates as a division of IXL. In February 2020 the platform recorded its 10 millionth hour of tutoring.

yemeksepeti.com.name: Yemeksepeti
yemeksepeti.com.description: Yemeksepeti runs an online ordering service in Türkiye, taking orders for restaurant delivery as well as groceries and everyday products. It was founded in 2001, and co-founder Nevzat Aydın was chief executive when Delivery Hero bought the company in 2015 in a deal reported at $589 million, then described as the largest acquisition in the region's internet sector. In July 2026 Delivery Hero agreed to sell Yemeksepeti to SSW Partners as part of Uber's planned takeover of Delivery Hero. That sale is expected to close in the second half of 2027, subject to regulatory approval.
yemeksepeti.com.status: Active. Agreed in July 2026 to be sold by Delivery Hero to SSW Partners, pending completion of Uber's takeover of Delivery Hero (expected second half of 2027)

yoco.com.name: Yoco
yoco.com.description: Yoco sells card machines, point of sale software and online payment tools to small and independent businesses in South Africa. Its range includes the Khumo card machines, Tap to Pay on iPhone, payment links and invoices, as well as Yoco Capital funding and a savings product. Katlego Maphai, Carl Wazen, Bradley Wattrus and Lungisa Matshoba started the company in Cape Town in 2013, and it says more than 200,000 merchants use its services. Carsten Höltkemeyer, who previously ran Solaris and Barclaycard's German business, became chief executive in June 2026.

yulu.bike.name: Yulu
yulu.bike.description: Yulu rents out small electric two-wheelers through its app, both for short city trips and on longer plans used by delivery riders working for ecommerce platforms. Founded in Bengaluru in 2017 by Amit Gupta, Naveen Dachuri, Anuj Tewari and RK Misra, it runs its shared service in 12 metro cities and in eight regional markets operated by franchisees. Bajaj Auto and Magna International led its Series B, and in August 2026 it raised $93 million in a Series C led by GEF Capital Partners. Operating revenue for FY25 was ₹237.4 crore.

zeptonow.com.name: Zepto
zeptonow.com.description: Zepto runs a quick commerce app in India that delivers groceries, fresh produce, snacks and household items from its own network of dark stores. It was set up by Aadit Palicha and Kaivalya Vohra and is based in Mumbai. According to its IPO filings it operates 1,139 dark stores across 66 cities and employs more than 5,200 permanent staff alongside about 48,000 operating staff. The market regulator SEBI approved its planned share listing on the NSE and BSE in May 2026, after the company moved its domicile from Singapore back to India.
zeptonow.com.status: Active. SEBI approved its IPO in May 2026, shares not yet listed

zerodha.com.name: Zerodha
zerodha.com.description: Zerodha is a Bengaluru stockbroker that lets Indian investors trade shares and derivatives online and invest in direct mutual funds. Brothers Nithin Kamath and Nikhil Kamath started it in August 2010, and the business is still run by the two founders. Its products include the Kite trading platform, the Coin mutual fund app, the Console back office and Kite Connect APIs, along with the free Varsity learning modules. The company says it has more than 18 million clients and accounts for over 15% of retail trading volumes in India. It is registered with SEBI as a broker and depository participant through Zerodha Broking Limited.

zipcar.com.name: Zipcar
zipcar.com.description: Zipcar runs a membership car-sharing service in which members book vehicles through a mobile app and pay only for the time they use. Robin Chase and Antje Danielson founded it in Cambridge, Massachusetts in 2000, and Avis Budget Group completed its purchase of the company in March 2013. Alongside personal memberships it runs Zipcar for Business and Zipcar for Universities programmes, and it says it has more than a million members. In 2026 Zipcar closed its UK operations, and Avis folded the Boston head office into the group's base in northern New Jersey while local services continued.
zipcar.com.status: Active. Ended UK operations in early 2026

zocdoc.com.name: Zocdoc
products: Zo AI phone assistant for practices
zocdoc.com.description: Zocdoc runs an online marketplace in the United States where patients look for doctors and other healthcare providers who accept their insurance, then book in-person or virtual appointments. Its network covers more than 200,000 providers across over 200 specialties and 10,000 insurance plans. Cyrus Massoumi, Oliver Kharraz and Nick Ganju founded the company in New York in 2007, and Kharraz is chief executive. In 2026 Zocdoc added booking inside Yelp and Google's Gemini app, and in October it completed its first acquisition, the insurance verification startup Sohar Health.

zoopla.co.uk.name: Zoopla
products: Homes for sale and rent listings
Zoopla for Business and ZooplaPro agent tools
zoopla.co.uk.description: Zoopla is a UK property portal listing homes for sale and to rent from estate and letting agents, with free online valuations that owners use to track what their home is worth. Alex Chesterman and Simon Kain founded it in 2007. It is part of Houseful, the property division of the former Zoopla Property Group, which private equity firm Silver Lake bought for £2.2 billion in 2018. Zoopla says more than six million homeowners now track their property's value on the site, and Paul Whitehead became its chief executive in 2025.
